entry_phrase: The `is_named_moderator` resolution is the **primitive** this gate consumes; the **gate itself** — admission check *plus* federation-path re-check — is **substrate**, not detector or consumer filter policy ([CC 4.4](part_4_composition_governance.md)).

gist: A member's content mass w_i is the L1 norm of its resampled payload; W is the fold's total; a census composite assigns unit mass per owner
entry_phrase: A member's **content mass** is an integer: `w_i`, the L1 norm of its payload on the resample basis of the fold (the sum of the byte values of the resampled payload, each `0..255`). `W = Σ w_i` is the mass of the fold. This is the mass of a content fold; a census composite assigns unit mass per owner ([CC 6.1.9](#6.1.9)).

gist: n_eff = floor((sum m_i)^2 / sum m_i^2) over committed fixed-point masses m_i greater than 0
entry_phrase: n_eff = floor( (Σ m_i)² / Σ m_i² )   over committed masses m_i > 0,

gist: An aggregator signs the n_eff it computes over the committed m_i, never one computed over w_i or any real-valued share
entry_phrase: An aggregator MUST sign the `n_eff` it computes over the committed `m_i`, never one computed over `w_i` or any real-valued share.

gist: A fold of more than 10^6 sources is refused at the door (fold_source_count_exceeded); larger populations fold hierarchically
entry_phrase: This edition pins a per-fold ceiling of 10⁶ sources, refused at the door above it (`fold_source_count_exceeded`). A larger population folds hierarchically, as a fold of folds, so `n_eff` never collapses to zero by encoding.

gist: An empty or all-zero-mass fold has n_eff = 0 (fail-closed); n_eff is in the signing preimage and a lying n_eff is checkable exactly against mass_commitment
entry_phrase: An empty or all-zero-mass fold has `n_eff = 0` (fail-closed: no positive mass, no effective sources). `n_eff` is a member of the signing preimage ([CC 6.1.2.1](#6.1.2.1)), so the value a verifier reads is the value the aggregator signed. A *lying* `n_eff` is **checkable against `mass_commitment` from held evidence exactly** — a verifier recomputes the floor over the committed integer masses, and any difference is the lie.

gist: A tier passes the mass-dominance gate iff version = 3, source_count greater than 0 and n_eff times 2 is at least source_count (min_ratio = 0.5)
entry_phrase: A tier passes the mass-dominance gate iff `version = 3`, `source_count > 0`, and

gist: min_ratio = 0.5 is CEG-pinned, not a tunable knob; two conformant substrates never disagree on which folds are admissible; no IEEE-754 path is used
entry_phrase: No IEEE-754 path is used here, as nowhere in this section. `min_ratio = 0.5` is **CEG-pinned** — a normative constant, not an implementation-tunable knob (two conformant substrates MUST NOT disagree on which folds are admissible).

gist: The dominance gate runs after signature verification and before persistence at aggregated-tier admission; a failing tier is rejected as aggregation_meta_dominated
entry_phrase: The gate MUST run **after** signature verification (which authenticates the `n_eff` it reads) and **before persistence** at aggregated-tier admission. A failing tier is rejected with the stable token `aggregation_meta_dominated`.

gist: max_source_multiplicity and mass_commitment are pinned normative constants, not tunable; the register pins the metric, threshold, clustering rule, n_min, leaf encoding and gate as one row
entry_phrase: They are therefore **pinned normative constants, not implementation-tunable knobs** — the same discipline as `min_ratio` above and the pinned `(R, ε)` default in [CC 6.1.2](#6.1.2). The register pins them as one row: the metric, the threshold, the clustering rule, `n_min`, the leaf encoding and the gate, with the inadmissibility of `version < 3`. A conformant implementation MUST use:

gist: Similarity = 1 minus normalized L1 distance over resampled payloads, in integer arithmetic; two members are joined iff similarity is strictly above threshold; an IEEE-754 decision path is never used
entry_phrase: - **similarity metric** — `1 − normalized L1 distance` over the resampled payloads: for two members `a`, `b` of resampled length `L`, `similarity = 1 − Σ|a_i − b_i| / (255 · L)`, evaluated **entirely in integer / fixed-point** arithmetic. Two members are joined by an edge of the similarity graph iff their similarity is **strictly above** the threshold, which in integers is `1000 · Σ|a_i − b_i| < (1000 − 950) · 255 · L`. An IEEE-754 decision path MUST NOT be used: it can fork admissibility between two honest implementations on byte-identical inputs.

gist: The similarity threshold is 0.950, carried as integer 950 milli-units
entry_phrase: - **threshold** — `0.950`, carried as the integer `950` in milli-units.

gist: Multiplicity is the largest connected component of the similarity graph (conservative superset of max-clique)
entry_phrase: - **clustering** — the largest **connected component** of the similarity graph. This is a deliberate conservative superset of the max-clique reading (max-clique is NP-hard); it can only **over**-estimate multiplicity, which only ever **tightens** the gate — the fail-safe direction for a privacy gate.

gist: Similarity is measured on the same nearest-neighbour resample the fold applies
entry_phrase: - **resample basis** — the **same** nearest-neighbour resample the fold applies; similarity MUST be measured on exactly the content the fold collapsed.

gist: n_min is substrate-side and corpus-kind-pinned (default 2) and is never producer-settable
entry_phrase: - **`n_min`** — substrate-side and corpus-kind-pinned (default `2`). It MUST NOT be producer-settable: a producer must not be able to widen its own admissibility.

gist: mass_commitment is the 6.1.1 Merkle root over leaves utf8(member_id) concatenated with u64 mass_to_fixed(w, W) = (2wE6 + W) div 2W; zero mass commits as 0; leaves sorted over raw bytes
entry_phrase: - **`mass_commitment`** — the [CC 6.1.1](#6.1.1) Merkle construction over per-member leaves `leaf_bytes = utf8(member_id) ‖ u64_be(mass_to_fixed(w_i, W))`, where the committed mass is the member's share of the fold's mass in micro-units, by integer division, nearest with ties rounded up: `mass_to_fixed(w, W) = (2 · w · 10⁶ + W) div (2 · W)` as a `u64`; a member with `w = 0`, or any member of a fold with `W = 0`, commits as `0`. As everywhere in the CC 6.1.1 scheme, leaves are sorted lexicographically over their **raw leaf bytes** before hashing (`leaf = SHA-256(leaf_bytes)`).

gist: A fold is multiplicity-admissible iff max_source_multiplicity times n_min is at most source_count
entry_phrase: - **gate** — a fold is multiplicity-admissible iff `max_source_multiplicity · n_min ≤ source_count`.

gist: Kish effective count k_eff = k / (1 + rho(k minus 1)) over k sources with average pairwise correlation rho
entry_phrase: The effective number of independent sources behind `k` distinct sources whose average pairwise correlation is `ρ̄` is the Kish effective count:

gist: An implementation clamps rho to [0,1] before applying it, so asserted anti-correlation never credits more than k
entry_phrase: An implementation MUST clamp `ρ̄` to `[0, 1]` before applying it. Positive semidefiniteness admits negative `ρ̄`, and the identity then yields `k_eff > k`. But asserted anti-correlation is exactly what an adversary fabricates to mint extra credit, so the clamp credits at most `k`.

gist: Fully correlated sources count as one (correlated-source discount); k_eff never falls below 1 and has ceiling 1/rho that scale cannot lift
entry_phrase: At `ρ̄ = 0`, `k_eff = k`; as the sources correlate, `k_eff` falls; at `ρ̄ → 1`, `k_eff → 1` and never below. **Fully correlated sources count as one** — this is the correlated-source discount. A clique of any size whose members move as one contributes at most one independent source, and no number of copies of one voice buys more. For `ρ̄ > 0` the count has a ceiling, `k_eff ≤ 1/ρ̄`, that scale cannot lift.

gist: rho is read from measured pairwise correlation (co-signing, shared steward lineage, temporal clustering) over attested event time, never over polling-window boundaries
entry_phrase: `ρ̄` is read from the pairwise correlation an implementation measures over its sources (co-signing frequency, shared steward lineage, temporal clustering — the [CC 3.1.8.4](part_3_the_namespace.md) F-3 matrix), over attested event time and never over polling-window boundaries.

gist: No operating band for rho or k_eff is pinned; an implementation may deny on low k_eff at its own threshold and must not grant on one
entry_phrase: This document pins no operating band for `ρ̄`, `k_eff` or any ratio derived from them. An implementation MAY deny on low `k_eff` at a threshold of its own and MUST NOT grant on one.

gist: n_eff (mass-weighted) and k_eff (correlation) are computed separately and never substituted for one another
entry_phrase: The mass-weighted `n_eff` above is Kish's other effective count, the weighting form over per-member masses. The two are computed separately and never substituted for one another.

gist: member_commitment commits to which members a tier folds, never to how much of the composite each supplies (mass) nor to how many members are the same content under different ids (multiplicity)
entry_phrase: `member_commitment` (CC 6.1.2.1.1) commits to *which* members a tier folds — never to *how much of the composite each supplies* (mass), nor to *how many members are the same content under different ids* (multiplicity).

gist: The signed n_eff and mass_commitment close the mass blindness; the signed max_source_multiplicity closes the multiplicity blindness
entry_phrase: The signed `n_eff` and `mass_commitment` close the first blindness; the signed `max_source_multiplicity` closes the second.

gist: The aggregator computes the effective source count at fold time from the per-member committed masses m_i, as the Kish / inverse-Simpson participation ratio taken to the integer floor
entry_phrase: The aggregator computes, at fold time, the **effective source count** of the tier from the per-member committed masses `m_i` — the Kish / inverse-Simpson participation ratio, taken to the integer floor over integer masses:

gist: The committed mass of the formula is m_i = mass_to_fixed(w_i, W)
entry_phrase: m_i = mass_to_fixed(w_i, W)

gist: The masses are the fixed-point integers mass_commitment commits, so aggregator and verifier compute over the same integers and no real number enters; the ratio is scale-free and under floor no tie is possible
entry_phrase: The masses are the fixed-point integers `mass_commitment` commits (`mass_to_fixed`, below), so aggregator and verifier compute over the same integers and no real number enters the computation. The ratio is scale-free, and under floor no tie is possible.

gist: A fold of N equal-mass sources has n_eff = N while each source's fixed-point mass is at least one unit: under the pinned micro-unit scale, for N up to 2 times 10^6 equal-mass sources
entry_phrase: A fold of N equal-mass sources has `n_eff = N` while the fixed-point mass of each source is at least one unit. Under the pinned micro-unit scale of `mass_to_fixed`, that holds for N ≤ 2·10⁶ equal-mass sources.

gist: Both (the micro-unit bound and the per-fold ceiling) are this edition's constants
entry_phrase: Both are this edition's constants.

gist: A fold where one source supplies about 90% of the composite collapses toward n_eff of 1
entry_phrase: A fold where one source supplies ~90% of the composite collapses toward `n_eff → 1`.

gist: The two Kish objects of the section are distinct: n_eff is a mass-weighted participation ratio over sources, k_eff the equicorrelated variance-of-mean count
entry_phrase: (The two "Kish" objects in this section are distinct: this `n_eff` is a mass-weighted participation ratio over sources; the `k_eff` of the effective-count paragraph at the end of this section is the equicorrelated variance-of-mean count.)

gist: The mass-dominance gate inequality is n_eff at least min_ratio times source_count, with pinned min_ratio = 0.5
entry_phrase: n_eff ≥ min_ratio · source_count      with pinned min_ratio = 0.5

gist: Over the committed integers the gate test is n_eff * 2 >= source_count, the exact integer form of min_ratio = 0.5
entry_phrase: Over the committed integers the test is `n_eff * 2 >= source_count`, the exact integer form of `min_ratio = 0.5`.

gist: max_source_multiplicity and mass_commitment are covered by the bound-hybrid signature, so a divergence in how they are computed is a fork in admissibility with valid signatures on both sides
entry_phrase: `max_source_multiplicity` and `mass_commitment` are covered by the bound-hybrid signature, so a divergence in how they are *computed* is not cosmetic: it is a fork in admissibility, with valid signatures on both sides.

gist: Cosine similarity is excluded by construction: byte vectors are all-positive, so even independent members score about 0.75
entry_phrase: (Cosine is excluded by construction — byte vectors are all-positive, so even independent members score ≈ 0.75.)

gist: Calibration of the threshold (to be replayed; the register row is staged): byte-identical 1.000, near-duplicate at least 0.99, independent high-entropy about 0.667
entry_phrase: Calibration (to be replayed; the register row is staged): byte-identical → `1.000`; near-duplicate → `≥ 0.99`; independent high-entropy → `≈ 0.667` (mean `|Δ|` of uniform bytes ≈ 85/255).

gist: mass_commitment makes a lying multiplicity provable from held evidence and a lying n_eff checkable exactly, since n_eff is the floor over the committed integers
entry_phrase: It makes a lying multiplicity provable from held evidence, and a lying `n_eff` checkable exactly, since `n_eff` is the floor over these committed integers.

gist: The R9 negative: 900 near-duplicate contents under 900 distinct ids at equal mass are mass-honest (n_eff == N, admitted by the dominance gate) and rejected only by the multiplicity gate, which is why a mass-only surface is insufficient; the replayed vector is staged in the register
entry_phrase: The R9 negative these constants make derivable from this document (the replayed vector is staged in the register) is 900 near-duplicate contents folded under 900 distinct ids at equal mass. They are perfectly mass-honest (`n_eff == N`, so the dominance gate admits them) and are rejected only by the multiplicity gate. That is why a mass-only surface is insufficient.

gist: The R9 constants close the wire-visibility half of the R9 residual and do not close the adversary-model limb of the 6.1.2 below-floor MUST, which remains unverifiable pending an instrument
entry_phrase: This closes the wire-visibility half of the R9 residual; it does **not** close the adversary-model limb of the [CC 6.1.2](#6.1.2) below-floor MUST, which remains unverifiable-pending-instrument.

gist: The Kish effective count formula k_eff = k / (1 + rho (k - 1))
Because rho is an average, a tight clique among independent sources is under-penalised: a computed k_eff can overstate effective diversity and never understates it
entry_phrase: Because `ρ̄` is an average, a tight clique embedded among independent sources is under-penalised: a computed `k_eff` can **overstate** effective diversity and never understates it.

gist: The register pins the proof of the effective count: the definition, its bounds, its monotone decrease in rho, the ceiling, and that a fully correlated clique counts as one
entry_phrase: The register pins the proof: the definition, its bounds, its monotone decrease in `ρ̄`, the ceiling, and that a fully correlated clique counts as one.

gist: The per-item target and chunk replication are available at every tier; anti-entropy is the standard carrier at every tier
entry_phrase: The per-item target of [CC 6.1.5.1](#6.1.5.1) and the chunk replication of this section are **available at every tier**. **Anti-entropy is the standard carrier at every tier**.

gist: Every row and blob of a cohort a node serves arrives by pull anti-entropy on the one carrier, never push, never waiting on a user; at federation scope rounds run among serve seats and a person's node takes from the commons what 5.2 says moves
entry_phrase: Every row and every blob of a cohort a node serves reaches it by **pull anti-entropy** on the one replication carrier — never by push, and never waiting on a user's action.

gist: No tier is exempt from anti-entropy except the opt-in anonymous tier, which may truly disappear
entry_phrase: No tier is exempt except the opt-in anonymous tier, which SR-2 above lets truly disappear.

gist: A holding claim and a custody:ack exist at every tier at the content's scope and reach the audience 5.2 gives that scope and no one else
entry_phrase: A holding claim (chunk level, [CC 6.1.5](#6.1.5)) and a `custody:ack:v1` report (whole blob, [CC 3.1.3.3](part_3_the_namespace.md)) exist at every tier, placed at the content's own scope. Both reach the audience [CC 5.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.2) gives that scope and no one else

gist: N6 possession-challengeability applies within the cohort exactly as outside it
entry_phrase: N6 (possession-challengeable claims) applies within the cohort exactly as outside it.

gist: Every CIRIS node is claimed (carries a live owner-binding to a person) before it operates on the mesh in normal operation
entry_phrase: Every CIRIS node is **claimed** before it operates on the mesh in normal operation — it carries a live owner-binding to a person ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md)).

gist: A node's audience is its owner's cohorts: a claimed node is in a cohort's audience only through its owner's membership; an unclaimed node is in none
entry_phrase: A node's audience is **its owner's cohorts**. A claimed node is in a cohort's audience only because its owner is a member of that cohort, and an unclaimed node is in no cohort's audience.

gist: An owner chooses per node which cohorts it serves; a denied node is outside that cohort's audience: not counted, no deficit, no keys, nothing pulled, enforced at both ends
entry_phrase: The owner then **chooses, per node, which of their cohorts it serves**: an allow list over the cohorts the owner belongs to ("don't replicate that community's content onto my work laptop").

gist: The per-node policy sits at the owner's self scope; each cohort sees only its own projection; a node receives only its own allowlist; a peer never sees a denied node
entry_phrase: (1) The owner's per-node policy is held at the owner's `self` scope.

gist: Every node a person owns is one of their devices: claiming it makes it an occurrence of their identity
entry_phrase: Every node a person owns **is one of that person's devices** ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.2)). Claiming it makes it an occurrence of their identity ([CC 3.3.6](part_3_the_namespace.md)), whatever it is for.

gist: A personal node defaults to all its owner's cohorts; a server node gets only the cohorts it serves, never self or family; the allow list is the consent:replication cohorts member
entry_phrase: A node is set up as **personal** by default, and a personal node's allow list is all of its owner's cohorts. A node set up as a **server** — managed, infrastructure, or serving a community or an affiliation — has an allow list of only the cohorts it was set up to serve. So the owner's `self` and `family` content does not follow them onto it: signing in at work, or claiming a work server, never copies a family's photos there.

gist: A replication flow proceeds only when it conforms on all five axes (sender, dimension and plane, cohort roster, consent:replication plus key grant, subject); an unlisted node simply holds no grant
entry_phrase: A flow proceeds only when it conforms on all of them. A node outside a cohort's allow list simply **holds no grant** for that cohort's rows.

gist: Two classes of self row reach a node regardless of its allow list: rows that originate on the node, and rows that refer to it
entry_phrase: Two classes of `self` row reach a node **regardless of its allow list**, each on an axis that already exists, and together they are what "the requisite for that node" means:

gist: A row naming the node (attested_key_id, subject_key_ids) or a grant issued for it (owner-binding, key record, config, consent, budget, revocation) is always served to it
entry_phrase: A row whose `attested_key_id` or `subject_key_ids` names the node, or a grant issued `for` it — its owner-binding, its key record, its `config:*` rows ([CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md), written by the owner about the node), its consent grants, its storage budget, its revocation — is always served to it.

gist: Changing a node's role edits its allow list: narrowing withdraws grants and the node descends what it lost; widening issues them and anti-entropy fills it
entry_phrase: *Changing a node's role is an edit to its allow list.* Narrowing withdraws the grants, and the node descends what it no longer has a grant for. Widening issues them, and anti-entropy fills it.

gist: An item's target holder count is counted over the content's audience (claimed nodes its scope entitles under their owners' choices) and capped by it
entry_phrase: An item's target holder count is counted over the content's **audience** — the claimed nodes its scope entitles to hold it under their owners' choices, as above — and is capped by it.

gist: Where the audience is smaller than the target, the target is the audience: every audience node holds the item, chunks still sealed
entry_phrase: Where the audience is smaller than the owner's target, the target is **the audience**: every audience node holds the item, and the replication factor is the audience size. The chunks are still sealed per [CC 5.4.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md).

gist: Where the audience is at least the target, the owner's target or the cohort's default (which a node must hold at) applies at every tier, rarest chunk first
entry_phrase: Where the audience is at least the target, the owner's target — or the cohort's default, which a node MUST be able to hold at — applies at every tier alike, and placement is rarest chunk first across the live cohort.

gist: Rarest-first, repair on loss, B2 pin-on-consent and B5 arbitration run at every tier; self and family budgets stay enforced locally only
entry_phrase: Rarest-first placement, repair on loss, B2 pin-on-consent and B5 arbitration run at every tier. B3 budgets for `self` / `family` stay enforced locally only, as [CC 6.1.5.2](#6.1.5.2) requires.

gist: Consent is supreme at every tier: N5 forces descent of withdrawn or revoked content regardless of rarity, pin or target
entry_phrase: Consent is supreme at every tier: N5 forces descent of withdrawn or revoked content regardless of rarity, pin or target.

gist: A node never holds content it is not party to; durability grows by a member claiming another node into the cohort, never by placing ciphertext on outsiders
entry_phrase: A node never holds content it is not party to. Durability therefore grows by a member **claiming another node** and admitting it to the cohort, never by placing a cohort's ciphertext on outsiders.

gist: Sealed self or family chunks are never held on nodes outside the cohort, even as indistinguishable ciphertext
entry_phrase: Sealed self/family chunks are not held on nodes outside the cohort, although such holders would see only indistinguishable ciphertext and durability would extend past the cohort.

gist: CC 5.4.2 seals self and family records chunk by chunk; the rules of this section give those tiers holding claims, rarest-first, repair and a measurable target
entry_phrase: [CC 5.4.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md) seals self/family records chunk by chunk. The rules below give those tiers holding claims, rarest-first, repair and a measurable target.

gist: At self and family scope the anti-entropy rounds run among the cohort's own nodes: a person's occurrences and the nodes they own; the family roster's devices
entry_phrase: At `self` and `family` scope the rounds run among the **cohort's own nodes** (a person's occurrences and the nodes they own; the family roster's devices).

gist: At self and family scope the rounds run over the derived plane or a direct link and, where no direct path exists, the 5.4.6 identity-link fallback
entry_phrase: At those two scopes they run over the derived plane or a direct link and, where no direct path exists, the [CC 5.4.6](part_5_transport_substrate.md) identity-link fallback.

gist: At community and affiliations scope the rounds run over the cohort roster
entry_phrase: At `community` / `affiliations` they run over the cohort roster.

gist: At federation scope the rounds run among serve seats over the commons, and a person's node takes from the commons what 5.2 says moves to a peer
entry_phrase: At federation scope they run among serve seats over the commons, and a person's node takes from the commons what [CC 5.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.2) says moves to a peer.

gist: A bounded cohort's holding claims and custody reports stay among its members' nodes; the Commons' are the holder directory
entry_phrase: a bounded cohort's stay among its members' nodes, and the Commons' are the holder directory ([CC 3.1.3.3](part_3_the_namespace.md))

gist: A home node is not a special case: it is a claimed node of its owner and through that claim holds what its owner's cohorts hold
entry_phrase: A home node is therefore not a special case. It is a claimed node of its owner, and through that claim it holds what its owner's cohorts hold.

gist: Three constraints keep the owner's per-node choice from leaking

gist: A holding claim is never a content binding: a withdrawn or tombstoned blob is not live because a device holds it; the bytes-plane fold reads liveness from content rows.
entry_phrase: a withdrawn or tombstoned blob is not live because a device still reports holding it ([CC 2.3](part_2_the_grammar.md) bytes plane). The bytes-plane fold MUST read liveness from the content's own rows only.

gist: A device ends its own custody report by re-acknowledging none or by withdraws; nobody withdraws another device's report; a takedown is the tombstone path.
entry_phrase: A device ends its own report by re-acknowledging `none` or by `withdraws`; nobody withdraws another device's report, and a takedown is the [CC 2.3](part_2_the_grammar.md) tombstone path, not a withdrawal of holders.

gist: A custody report's freshness is the row's own expires_at (72 hours); no second TTL exists.
entry_phrase: The 72-hour window below is the claim's `expires_at`; no second TTL exists.

gist: A custody report is live for 72 hours; a responsive device re-acknowledges about daily; older than 72 hours reads as unknown; a device that drops a blob re-acknowledges none.
entry_phrase: A report is **live for 72 hours** from its instant, and a responsive device re-acknowledges about **daily**. A report older than 72 hours reads as *unknown*

gist: Per device a member sees here, received, none or unknown; known copies is the count of here; a UI MUST NOT show unknown as none or lapsed here as copy.
entry_phrase: The count of *here* is the number of known copies; a UI MUST NOT present *unknown* as *none*, nor a lapsed `here` as a copy.

gist: A here report is trusted as signed by the device; no possession challenge exists yet.
entry_phrase: A `here` report is trusted as signed by the device: nothing on the wire yet asks the device to prove it still holds the bytes. Possession challenges for custody reports are not yet defined.

gist: A holding claim counted toward rarity weighs by what backs it (possession verified 2, signature only 1, unverified 0); a custody report is a separate within-cohort count, not possession-bound.
entry_phrase: until a challenger exists a holding claim weighs by what backs it (possession verified 2, signature only 1, unverified 0). No challenger is defined in this edition. A custody report is a separate, within-cohort count and is not thereby a possession-bound claim.

gist: A family must be able to see how many copies of its content exist without weakening encryption or outsider invisibility.
entry_phrase: A family must be able to see how many copies of its content exist

gist: No row shape exists that could advertise a bounded cohort's holdings to outsiders.
entry_phrase: so no row shape exists that could advertise a bounded cohort's holdings to outsiders.

gist: Scope paragraph names the content's own cohort_scope as self for a person's own devices, family, or community.
entry_phrase: A custody report is placed at the content's own `cohort_scope` by rule (1) below

gist: The blob's name and format stay in the sealed descriptor; an outsider learns nothing it did not learn before.
entry_phrase: the blob's name and format stay in the sealed descriptor ([CC 3.3.13](part_3_the_namespace.md)). An outsider learns nothing it did not learn before.

gist: A report's scope is self, family, community or affiliations for a bounded cohort.
entry_phrase: A report is placed at the `cohort_scope` of the blob it is about: `self`, `family`, `community` or `affiliations` for a bounded cohort

gist: At a bounded scope the here rows are the within-cohort custody view and nothing else.
entry_phrase: at a bounded scope they are the within-cohort custody view and nothing else.

gist: A holding claim says where bytes are, not that they may stay.
entry_phrase: It says where bytes are, not that they may stay

gist: Holding claims at every tier, bounded to the cohort, is true at every tier with no exception clause.
entry_phrase: is true at every tier with no exception clause.

gist: A lost device stops counting within three days, while a phone off for a weekend still counts.
entry_phrase: a lost device stops counting within three days, while a phone that is off for a weekend still counts.

gist: A device that drops a blob re-acknowledges none.
entry_phrase: A device that drops a blob re-acknowledges `none`.

gist: The four per-device states: here is a live here report; received is a delivery receipt with no later live report; none is a live none report; unknown is no live report.
entry_phrase: - **received** — a [CC 5.3.3.6](part_5_transport_substrate.md) delivery receipt with no later live report;

gist: Named residual: a device that lies or whose storage has silently rotted is counted as a copy until its report lapses or it is challenged once challenges exist.
entry_phrase: is counted as a copy until its report lapses or it is challenged once challenges exist.

gist: N6 of CC 6.1.5 is unchanged and still governs a holding claim counted toward an item's rarity.
entry_phrase: CC 6.1.5's **N6** is unchanged and still governs a holding claim counted toward an item's rarity

gist: The at-rest DEK cascade is substrate-wraps-by-default: the substrate generates the per-write DEK and wraps it to each active recipient's x25519 and ML-KEM-768 keys resolved by key_id
entry_phrase: the substrate generates the per-write DEK and wraps it to each active recipient

gist: Recipients must register encryption keys via encryption_pubkeys because the key registration carries only signing keys and ML-KEM cannot be derived from ML-DSA
entry_phrase: So recipients must register encryption keys, and the substrate must resolve them by `key_id`.

gist: An encryption_pubkeys binding is admitted only when attesting_key_id is the identity_key_id or a current occurrence of it (self-certified)
entry_phrase: admitted only when `attesting_key_id == identity_key_id` (or a current occurrence of it)

gist: The encryption_pubkeys binding is hybrid-signed (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65)
entry_phrase: **Hybrid-signed** (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65) — the binding itself is PQC-signed.

gist: KEM keys rotate by a new identity_occurrence superseding the prior, without touching the stable signing key_id; encryption keys are not a field on the key record
entry_phrase: a new `identity_occurrence` superseding the prior rotates the KEM keys **without touching the stable signing `key_id`**

gist: identity_occurrence is its own kind in the replication wire; encryption pubkeys replicate in cleartext inside the occurrence envelope; no new replication kind
entry_phrase: `identity_occurrence` is its own kind in the locked replication wire, so the encryption pubkeys propagate inside the occurrence envelope that already replicates — **no new replication kind, no Edge wire change**.

gist: Signing, RET-transport and content-KEM are three distinct keypairs; deriving the content-KEM x25519 from either other is a conformance violation; the transport key never wraps content DEKs
entry_phrase: Deriving the content-KEM x25519 from either of the others is a conformance violation (cross-protocol key reuse).

gist: When an identity_occurrence carries both encryption_pubkeys and transport_destination the substrate MUST reject at admission if the content x25519 equals reticulum_x25519_pubkey; signing-key reuse stays a producer-side obligation
entry_phrase: the substrate MUST **reject at admission** if `encryption_pubkeys.x25519_base64` decodes to the same 32 bytes as `transport_destination.reticulum_x25519_pubkey`

gist: KEM-key rotation bounds future exposure only; after a compromise operators MUST treat content whose DEKs were wrapped to that key as exposed and MAY re-encrypt; no automatic trigger
entry_phrase: Operators with a compromised-key event MUST treat all content whose DEKs were wrapped to that key as exposed, and MAY re-encrypt.

gist: A wrap target is resolved from the current (non-superseded, within valid_until) identity_occurrence for that key_id and its encryption_pubkeys
entry_phrase: reads the **current (non-superseded, within-`valid_until`) `identity_occurrence` for that `key_id` → its `encryption_pubkeys`**

gist: A recipient whose current occurrence has no valid ML-KEM-768 key is fail-secure excluded; the substrate MUST NOT fall back to plaintext or v1; recipients MUST have an occurrence with encryption_pubkeys
entry_phrase: the substrate MUST NOT fall back to plaintext or to v1

gist: A family member named only by key_id with no occurrence is excluded from wraps: no presence, no wrap target
entry_phrase: no presence ⇒ no wrap target ⇒ excluded

gist: encryption_pubkeys is one optional field-set on identity_occurrence; no new subject_kind or replication kind
entry_phrase: `encryption_pubkeys` is one optional field-set on the existing `identity_occurrence` subject_kind

gist: the transport key never wraps content DEKs; the federation seed never enters the transport layer
entry_phrase: the federation seed never enters the transport layer, and the transport key never wraps content DEKs

gist: Recovering historical content after a KEM-key compromise requires DEK rotation and re-encryption, which CEG does not mandate
entry_phrase: **Recovering historical content after a KEM-key compromise requires DEK rotation + content re-encryption under the new DEK — which CEG does NOT mandate.**

gist: KEM rotation is not to be represented as recovering confidentiality of previously-wrapped content
entry_phrase: Do not represent KEM rotation as recovering the confidentiality of previously-wrapped content.

gist: To be an at-rest-encryption recipient an identity MUST have a federation-present identity_occurrence carrying encryption_pubkeys
entry_phrase: an identity MUST have a federation-present `identity_occurrence` carrying `encryption_pubkeys`

gist: Reuse of the signing key as KEM key is not wire-checkable and remains a producer-side conformance obligation
entry_phrase: remains a producer-side conformance obligation

gist: organization, org_membership and partner_record are retired; no substrate admits them as record kinds; their names stay only so citations resolve
entry_phrase: The three kinds below are retired by amendment ([CC 4.5.1](part_4_composition_governance.md)): their names stay in this section so citations resolve, no substrate admits them as record kinds, and everything they carried lives on the affiliation record.

gist: An organisation is a community at cohort_scope affiliations: org_id is community_key_id, parent is hierarchy nesting, member is a membership seat, role a delegates_to scope set, partner licensure
entry_phrase: The Portal's `Organization` is a community at `cohort_scope: affiliations` ([CC 4.4.3.2.8](part_4_composition_governance.md)) and nothing about an organisation is a record kind of its own:

gist: Founding an affiliation is self-founding under the founder's key; no administrator's door and no roster of permitted authorities
entry_phrase: founding is self-founding under the founder's key — no administrator's door, no roster of permitted authorities.

gist: A delegated holder never stands in for the consensus_protocol on a roster or config change; roster events stay cosigned; a keyless affiliation's key manager holds registration under quorum cosignature
entry_phrase: A delegated holder never stands in for the `consensus_protocol` on a roster or config change (roster events stay cosigned under the protocol), and a keyless affiliation's key manager holds the registration binding under the quorum's cosignature.

gist: An organisation naming an employee as its agent's steward takes on the charter duty not to punish that steward for refusing an unlawful or unsafe instruction or recording a refusal
entry_phrase: It is the duty not to punish that steward for refusing an unlawful or unsafe instruction about the agent, and not to discipline a refusal that the steward records with its reason.

gist: An affiliation record and a licence carry only what the federation needs cross-region; PII and business detail never federate; minimisation is the emitter's discipline, the substrate is no PII filter
entry_phrase: An affiliation record and a licence carry only what the federation needs to enforce trust and authorization cross-region; PII and business detail stay in the issuer's own store and never federate. Minimisation is the emitter's discipline; the substrate admits and merges what is signed and is not a PII filter.

gist: Neither an affiliation record nor a licence carries payment-processor-derived data in any member; a substrate MUST refuse a row carrying a recognizable payment-processor identifier
entry_phrase: Neither row carries payment-processor-derived data (customer ids, subscription ids, charge refs, card metadata), including through any open-vocabulary member; a substrate MUST refuse a row carrying a recognizable payment-processor identifier.

gist: A licence from an organisation is admitted only when its signature set resolves to the affiliation's key set under its consensus_protocol; a single key MUST NOT issue one; JCS-sorted members
entry_phrase: A licence issued by an organisation is admitted only when its signature set resolves to the affiliation's key set under its `consensus_protocol` (the paragraph below; the [CC 3.2](#3.2) founder-quorum machinery); a signature set short of that protocol MUST NOT issue one, and one key suffices only where the protocol says so.

gist: A licence carries a monotonic revision; admission refuses a decrease and the check precedes the merge so a stale active never overwrites a revocation
entry_phrase: A licence carries a monotonic `revision`; admission refuses a decrease, and the check precedes the merge, so a stale `active` never overwrites a revocation.

gist: Licence current state resolves by stable-id grouping: supersedes to amend, withdraws to revoke, latest asserted_at, tie-break smallest attestation_id; chain completeness never required
entry_phrase: Current state is resolved by stable-id grouping, `supersedes` to amend and `withdraws` to revoke, and never requires chain completeness.

gist: The operational layer moves only as signed envelopes; no cross-region byte moves outside one
entry_phrase: the federation's own operational layer still moves only as signed envelopes: no cross-region byte moves outside one ([CC 1.7](part_1_foundation.md)).

gist: When a licensing authority is an organisation the authority_id of licensure:{authority_id} is the affiliation's community_key_id, not a legal registration number; names the key set, not who may
entry_phrase: When a licensing authority is an organisation, the `authority_id` segment of `licensure:{authority_id}` is the affiliation's `community_key_id`, **not** a legal registration number (jurisdiction-scoped, mutable, PII-adjacent).

gist: An organisation that names an employee-steward takes the duty on in its affiliation charter
entry_phrase: An organisation that names an employee as the steward of its agent takes on, in its affiliation charter, a duty toward that steward.

gist: The steward's name on the record is the organisation's accountability, not its shield
entry_phrase: The steward's name on the record is the organisation's accountability, not its shield.

gist: org_id is community_key_id; parent_org_id is hierarchy nesting; org_type is affiliation_archetype + membership_basis
entry_phrase: - `org_type` is `affiliation_archetype` + `membership_basis`;

gist: A member is a membership:{stage} seat
entry_phrase: - a member is a `membership:{stage}` seat ([CC 3.1.3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md));

gist: A role is a delegates_to edge in the hierarchy whose scope set names what the member may do; the four role names are non-normative presets; admin scopes are open vocabulary published as data
entry_phrase: - a role is a `delegates_to` edge in the `hierarchy` whose `scope` set names what the member may do. `OrgAdmin` / `KeyManager` / `Operator` / `Viewer` are non-normative presets over scope sets. Admin scopes are open vocabulary, their canonical presets published as data with the family model manifest rather than listed here;

gist: A partner is licensure:{community_key_id}:v1 with partner_role:{role} for the tier and duty:{kind} for obligations
entry_phrase: - a partner is `licensure:{community_key_id}:v1` with `partner_role:{role}` for the tier and `duty:{kind}` for obligations;

gist: CIRIS L3C is one such affiliation and uses the same rows
entry_phrase: CIRIS L3C is one such affiliation and uses the same rows.

gist: Informative: what each retired kind carried; each rode scores with a subject_kind discriminator at the Commons tier, PII held off the wire in the issuer's per-region store
entry_phrase: Each rode `scores` with a subject_kind discriminator at the Commons tier, the issuer's own per-region store holding every piece of PII and business detail off the wire.

gist: The replication wire tokens organization, org_membership, partner_record name nothing a substrate admits
entry_phrase: The replication wire tokens `organization` · `org_membership` · `partner_record` name nothing a substrate admits.

gist: Billing stays off-wire
entry_phrase: Billing stays off-wire ([CC 3.3.10](#3.3.10)).

gist: A licence's set-valued members are lexicographically sorted by JCS string form so M signers produce byte-identical bytes
entry_phrase: are lexicographically sorted by JCS string form ([CC 2.6.1.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) rule 1) so M signers produce byte-identical bytes.

gist: The vector set includes the M-of-N identical-bytes round trip
entry_phrase: The vector set includes the M-of-N identical-bytes round trip.

gist: The admission quorum is distinct from the region merge quorum; the substrate's merge never counts signers
entry_phrase: This admission quorum is distinct from the region merge quorum of [CC 5.3.2.3](part_5_transport_substrate.md): the substrate's merge never counts signers.

gist: The community_key_id is the org_id the retired record carried, through which the organisation's keys resolve under its consensus_protocol
entry_phrase: That `community_key_id` is the `org_id` the retired record carried, through which the organisation's keys resolve under its `consensus_protocol` ([CC 2.4.1.2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)).

gist: The segment names the key set an emitter must resolve to for its row to be the organisation's licensure rather than testimony about it
entry_phrase: The segment names the key set an emitter must resolve to for its row to be the organisation's licensure rather than testimony about it ([CC 2.4.1.2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)).

gist: Not a gate on who may be an authority: anyone may, under their own key
entry_phrase: This naming is not a gate on who may be an authority — anyone may, under their own key.

gist: cohort_scope is chosen per envelope by the emitter under the smallest-scope default; no self-report family is pinned to a scope
entry_phrase: `cohort_scope` is a **different axis**, chosen per envelope by the emitter under the [CC 1.13.3.4](part_1_foundation.md) smallest-scope default

gist: A config leaf whose content structural invisibility protects (admission, transport) MUST be emitted at self scope
entry_phrase: A leaf whose content is exactly what structural invisibility protects — `admission` (admin key ids), `transport` (bootstrap peers, peer sideband) — MUST be emitted at `self`.

gist: A bare operational config leaf (load) MAY be emitted at the smallest scope reaching peers that route to it; never federation by reflex, federation only for a commons-serving node
entry_phrase: Such a leaf MAY be emitted at the **smallest scope that reaches the peers which route to it** — never federation by reflex, and federation only for a node serving the commons.

gist: An emission grant (infra:attest) confers authority to emit and no right to be believed; a delegation is never an input to a receiver's trust set
entry_phrase: confers authority to **emit**, and confers **no right to be believed**. A grant issued by *my* owner cannot bind *your* composer.

gist: An unpinned peer's self-report is admissible but unweighted; a consumer MAY weight it from a relationship it already holds, as consumer policy
entry_phrase: A consumer MAY weight that self-report from a relationship it already holds: a peer the consumer replicates from is one whose claims *about itself* it has already decided to accept at some weight. That weighting is [CC 4.4](part_4_composition_governance.md) consumer policy, never a number this document sets.

gist: Absent trust or consent a claim reaches only its author; a self-report flows to a peer only where the producer's consent grant includes it and the recipient is entitled
entry_phrase: A self-report moves to a peer by the rule of [CC 5.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.2): the peer is in the row's audience, and the peer pulls it, must hold it, or the producer's consent grant covers it.

gist: A self-report that renews MUST carry supersedes against the row it replaces, so the live set is one row per (subject, scope, leaf)
entry_phrase: A self-report that renews to stay current MUST carry `supersedes` ([CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md)) against the row it replaces. The live set is thereby **one row per `(subject, scope, leaf)`**.

gist: A composer weighting self-attestations by live count MUST count distinct subjects, never distinct rows
entry_phrase: A composer weighting self-attestations by live count MUST therefore count **distinct subjects**, never distinct rows.

gist: Superseding is forward-only: it ends the prior row's liveness and does not un-say it
entry_phrase: Superseding is forward-only ([CC 4.5.9.3](part_4_composition_governance.md)): it does not un-say the prior record, it ends its liveness.

gist: Nothing in the document pins config:* or any self-report family to a cohort_scope; the CC 3.1.9 row constrains the subject only
entry_phrase: Nothing in this document pins `config:*` — or any self-report family — to a `cohort_scope`.

gist: A delegation that could add its holder to a stranger's trust set would be authority laundering; the CC 3.4.7.3 rule applies in the same shape
entry_phrase: A delegation that could add its holder to a stranger's trust set would be authority laundering, and the [CC 3.4.7.3](part_3_the_namespace.md) rule that neither party may assert the other's relation applies here in the same shape.

gist: Anyone may claim anything; absent trust or consent a claim reaches no one but its author
entry_phrase: **Anyone may claim anything; absent trust or consent, a claim reaches no one but its author.**

gist: The route is the consent-gated attestation plane, not a new namespace; it is consent plus trust
entry_phrase: The route a self-report actually travels is therefore the consent-gated attestation plane, not a new namespace.

gist: Open: whether an event kind is carried on a replication plane at all is an implementation's plane set, not a rule of the document
entry_phrase: Whether a given event kind is carried on a replication plane at all is an implementation's plane set, not a rule of this document.

gist: Carrying machine origin on a Contribution is mandatory, via the attesting key's role-set and the existing content_class vocabulary, with no new wire surface
entry_phrase: This section makes carrying machine origin **mandatory rather than incidental**.

gist: A Contribution carrying generated content MUST carry content_class:generated; one carrying materially altered content MUST carry content_class:generated_modified; this applies to any content including text
entry_phrase: A Contribution carrying generated content MUST carry `content_class:generated`; one carrying materially-altered content MUST carry `content_class:generated_modified`

gist: Where a sub_kind's Source struct carries the AI-generation disclosure field it MUST be populated; on an agent-attested Contribution an absent or unknown value MUST resolve to disclosed as generated
entry_phrase: that field MUST be populated. On an agent-attested Contribution an absent or unknown value of that field MUST resolve to *disclosed as generated*

gist: A Contribution carrying content generated by a CIRIS agent MUST be attested under a key whose identity_type contains agent; an agent MUST NOT publish generated content under a non-agent key
entry_phrase: A Contribution carrying content generated by a CIRIS agent MUST additionally be attested under a key whose `identity_type` ([CC 3.4.7.1](part_3_the_namespace.md)) contains `agent`. An agent MUST NOT publish generated content under a key that does not carry the `agent` role.

gist: A human publisher of AI-generated content stays the attester and still carries the content_class generation marking
entry_phrase: R1 remains binding on a human publisher of AI-generated content — the person's key stays the attester, and the class marking carries the origin.

gist: At egress to a non-CEG channel the emitting node MUST re-express the generation marking in the destination's machine-readable form: C2PA for generated media (now MUST), interaction disclosure for interactive text
entry_phrase: At a publish boundary where content leaves CEG for a non-CEG channel, the emitting node MUST re-express the marking in the destination's native machine-readable form. For media that form is the [CC 8.4.2.2](part_8_appendices.md) C2PA assertion (normative as of this section — that profile's `MAY` is promoted to `MUST` for generated media). For interactive text that form is the Art. 50(1) interaction-disclosure limb.

gist: Where a destination supports no machine-readable marking the node MUST still emit the human-legible disclosure and MUST record the gap as a hard_case:* observation naming the channel
entry_phrase: Where a destination channel supports NO machine-readable marking, the node MUST still emit the human-legible disclosure AND MUST record the gap as a `hard_case:*` observation naming the channel.

gist: A node MUST NOT strip a generation marking present on ingress
entry_phrase: A node MUST NOT strip a marking present on ingress.

gist: Assistive operations (spell-check, grammar, formatting, transcode) MUST NOT be marked as generated
entry_phrase: Assistive operations MUST NOT be marked.

gist: Generated content published unmarked by its generator, or a marking stripped at egress, is a false attestation: the substrate observes and emits hard_case:*, the WA quorum owns the verdict
entry_phrase: Generated content published without the R1 marking by the party that generated it is a false attestation on the existing evidence floor.

gist: A downstream republisher omitting a marking it never received is an observation about the ingress path, not a verdict; the generator is the duty-holder
entry_phrase: A downstream republisher that omits a marking it never received is an observation about the ingress path, not a verdict against the republisher: **the generator is the duty-holder**

gist: A CIRIS agent's federation identity is minted with identity_type containing agent, so every Contribution it attests is machine-origin by construction
entry_phrase: a CIRIS agent's federation identity is minted with `identity_type` containing `agent`, so every Contribution it attests is machine-origin by construction.

gist: The C2PA emit MUST ship in the same release that first publishes generated media; a deployment claiming conformance MUST name that release, resolved through the evidence registry, never by assertion
entry_phrase: it MUST ship in the same release that first publishes generated media. A deployment claiming CC conformance MUST be able to name the release in which its marking path ships. The claim resolves through the evidence registry, never by assertion

gist: Definitions: generated is content wholly or substantially produced by an AI system; materially altered is human-origin content whose meaning-bearing substance an AI system changed; assistive operations do not substantially alter their input and are not generation
entry_phrase: *Generated* — content wholly or substantially produced by an AI system. *Materially altered* — human-origin content whose meaning-bearing substance has been changed by an AI system (the Art. 50(4) deep-fake limb). *Assistive* — spell-check, grammar, formatting, transport re-encoding, lossless transcode, and other operations that do not substantially alter their input; explicitly NOT generation (R4).

gist: generated and generated_modified are canonical additions to the content_class open vocabulary, a documentation-only registry entry, not a new prefix
entry_phrase: These are canonical additions to that family's existing open vocabulary — a documentation-only registry entry per [CC 4.5.1.1](part_4_composition_governance.md) axis-vocabulary discipline, NOT a new prefix.

gist: content_class is not multimedia-scoped: it applies to any Contribution carrying content, text included
entry_phrase: **`content_class` is not multimedia-scoped**: it applies to any Contribution carrying content, text included

gist: Machine origin is determinable from the signed envelope alone by any reader; the marking is bound to the producer and revocable on the same handle as every other claim
entry_phrase: Machine origin is thereby determinable from the signed envelope alone, by any reader, without trusting a self-declared flag: the marking is cryptographically bound to the producer and revocable on the same handle as every other claim.

gist: An unmarkable channel is a recorded exception, never a silent drop
entry_phrase: An unmarkable channel is a recorded exception, never a silent drop.

gist: Reason for R4: marking everything is the same failure as marking nothing; the bound keeps the marking a signal
entry_phrase: Marking everything is the same failure as marking nothing: a disclosure that fires on every spell-check carries no information and trains readers to ignore it.

gist: The client renders agent-versus-human origin from the signed envelope
entry_phrase: The client renders agent-versus-human origin from the signed envelope — the disclosure *is* the attestation, read back, not a label the producer remembers to add.

gist: The R3 media form (C2PA emit) is normative wherever generated media is published
entry_phrase: The R3 media form ([CC 8.4.2.2](part_8_appendices.md) C2PA emit) is normative **wherever generated media is published**

gist: A conformance statement the pinned manifests cannot resolve is not one this document may cite
entry_phrase: a conformance statement the pinned manifests cannot resolve is not one this document may cite.

gist: accord:lifecycle:active is the only sanctioned resumption after a constitutional halt
entry_phrase: `accord:lifecycle:active` is the **only** sanctioned resumption after a `constitutional` halt ([CC 4.2.1](#4.2.1)).

gist: lifecycle:active is a cosigned row (additional_scrubs) by a strict majority of the standing roster; the quorum sits on the recoverable act, not the stop
entry_phrase: **It is a cosigned row by a strict majority of the standing roster** (`additional_scrubs[]`, [CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md)): the quorum sits on the recoverable act, not on the stop.

gist: lifecycle:confirmed rides the lifecycle domain with invocation_kind lifecycle:confirmed and confirms_halt_id in place of resumes_halt_id
entry_phrase: The confirmation is written `invocation_kind=lifecycle:confirmed`, with `confirms_halt_id=` in place of `resumes_halt_id=`.

gist: A confirmation after the fuse has lapsed confirms nothing; a fresh halt is fired instead
entry_phrase: A confirmation after the fuse has lapsed confirms nothing, and a fresh halt is fired instead.

gist: Lifecycle rows sign a separate canonical-bytes domain from accord:invoke; invoke's invocation_kind stays closed to constitutional, notify, drill so an invoke can never replay as a resumption nor the reverse
entry_phrase: The `accord:invoke` `invocation_kind` stays closed to `{constitutional, notify, drill}` (the scope-isolation rule — a fourth value is *not* added to it).
