gist: a withdraws signed by a federation-enrolled subject is admitted under rule 2
entry_phrase: **A `federation_keys.key_id`** — the subject is a federation-enrolled identity that can sign on its own behalf.

gist: a subject_key_ids entry may be a tagged canonical-hash identifier for an external party with no key record
entry_phrase: **A tagged canonical-hash identifier** — the subject is an external party with no federation_keys row (a platform user-id, channel-id, content-sha256-bound entity, etc.).

gist: revocation for a canonical-hash subject rides a delegates_to proxy chain under rule 3
entry_phrase: 2. **A tagged canonical-hash identifier** — the subject is an external party with no federation_keys row (a platform user-id, channel-id, content-sha256-bound entity, etc.). The substrate cannot verify a signature from this entity directly; **revocation rides a `delegates_to` proxy chain** under rule 3 of [CC 2.4.1.1](#2.4.1.1). Wire form: a tagged string per CC 2.3.2.1 below.

gist: both subject entry forms are admitted; the canonical-hash form is distinguished by its explicit tag
entry_phrase: Both forms are admitted; the canonical-hash variant is distinguished by its explicit tag ([CC 2.3.2.1](#2.3.2.1)).

gist: an enrolled key proxies an un-enrolled subject's revocation by a delegates_to from the canonical hash with scope consent_revocation; the subject never enrolls
entry_phrase: A federation-enrolled key (typically the agent holding data on behalf of the external party) carries `delegates_to(canonical_hash → agent_key, scope: [consent_revocation])`; the agent proxies revocation ([CC 2.4.1.1](#2.4.1.1)).

gist: canonical_binding: a now-enrolled key asserts it is the entity behind a canonical hash; after admission that key signs withdraws directly under rule 2
entry_phrase: - **`canonical_binding`** — *retroactive identity claim*. A now-enrolled federation key asserts "I AM the entity behind `canonical:sha256:{hex}`", binding past canonical-hash subject entries to its real identity. After an admitted `canonical_binding`, the formerly-un-enrolled subject can sign `withdraws` **directly** under rule (2) — the binding promotes the canonical-hash to a real key_id for admission purposes.

gist: canonical_binding is not a fifth admission rule; it is a delegates_to-shaped row with scope identity_binding, admitted because the key proves preimage control out of band
entry_phrase: It composes: the binding is itself a `delegates_to`-shaped attestation (`delegates_to(canonical_hash → newly_enrolled_key, scope: [identity_binding])`) admitted because the enrolling key proves control of the preimage out-of-band.

gist: the substrate admits each half of a bilateral partnership independently; ingest never enforces ratification
entry_phrase: Per [CC 3.3.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.5) step 4: a bilateral partnership is "ratified iff both halves present and live under the same `bilateral_pair_id` with `stance: granted`" — and this predicate is **consumer policy**, NOT registry-normative. Ingest-layer builders produce the two halves WITHOUT enforcing ratification. The substrate admits each half independently; composition of the pair into a ratified partnership is a downstream read-time computation, never an admission gate.

gist: bilateral ratification (both halves present under one bilateral_pair_id with stance granted) is consumer policy computed at read time, never an admission gate
entry_phrase: Per [CC 3.3.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.3.5) step 4: a bilateral partnership is "ratified iff both halves present and live under the same `bilateral_pair_id` with `stance: granted`" — and this predicate is **consumer policy**, NOT registry-normative. Ingest-layer builders produce the two halves WITHOUT enforcing ratification. The substrate admits each half independently; composition of the pair into a ratified partnership is a downstream read-time computation, never an admission gate.

gist: visibility is set producer-side by cohort_scope with family_id or community_id
entry_phrase: | **Visibility** | `cohort_scope` + (`family_id` or `community_id` when set) | Producer-side | Who can SEE the data |

gist: revocability is subject-side, by subject_key_ids
entry_phrase: | **Revocability** | `subject_key_ids` | Subject-side | Who can REVOKE the data |

gist: delivery is set by delivery_mode and history_on_join, substrate and subscriber side
entry_phrase: | **Delivery** | `delivery_mode` + `history_on_join` | Substrate / subscriber | Who actively RECEIVES the data + how the substrate fans out |

gist: subject-side revocation applies federation-wide regardless of the producer's occurrence_id; per-occurrence lifecycle consent is producer-side
entry_phrase: This orthogonality is load-bearing for the multi-occurrence consent shape: subject-side revocation applies federation-wide regardless of producer's `occurrence_id`; per-occurrence lifecycle consent is a producer-side concern, separately tracked.

gist: a row whose attesting_key_id is in subject_key_ids is a self-consent ceremony; an agent attests identity:current about itself with subject_key_ids = [self]
entry_phrase: This composes naturally with the CEG-native agent's self-attestation pattern: agent attests `identity:current` about itself with `subject_key_ids = [self.key_id]`, asserting consent-authority over its own identity claims.

gist: subject_key_ids is optional; each entry names a party with substrate-recognized authority over the row's continued processing
entry_phrase: When present, each entry names a party with substrate-recognized authority over this Contribution's continued processing ([CC 2.1](#2.1)).

gist: an empty subject_key_ids is the status quo, producer-only authority; subject authority is additive and never changes how a consumer reads a row that omits it
entry_phrase: `subject_key_ids` as `[]` in the mirror (the column beside the row absent) is the status-quo shape (producer-only authority; same as a baseline Contribution carrying no subject authority) ([CC 2.1](#2.1)). Consumers that don't read the field see status-quo behavior. Subject authority is additive at the envelope layer — adding it never changes how an existing consumer reads an envelope that omits it.

gist: delegates_to carries scope[], delegation_purpose, delegation_valid_from, delegation_valid_until; A authorizes B to sign for A within a bounded scope
entry_phrase: A authorizes B to sign on A's behalf within a bounded scope

gist: delegation_valid_until is REQUIRED and at most 365 days after valid_from on an edge carrying sub_delegation, license, grant, moderate, takedown, review or slash, or in an affiliation hierarchy
entry_phrase: `{scope[], delegation_purpose, delegation_valid_from, delegation_valid_until}` — `delegation_valid_until` is **REQUIRED, at most 365 days (365 × 86 400 s) after `delegation_valid_from`**, on any edge carrying `sub_delegation`, `license`, `grant`, `moderate`, `takedown`, `review` or `slash`, or sitting in an affiliation's `hierarchy` ([CC 4.4.3.2.8](part_4_composition_governance.md) C); a perpetual or over-ceiling edge is refused `delegation_term_required`;

gist: a perpetual or over-ceiling delegation edge needing a term is refused delegation_term_required
entry_phrase: `{scope[], delegation_purpose, delegation_valid_from, delegation_valid_until}` — `delegation_valid_until` is **REQUIRED, at most 365 days (365 × 86 400 s) after `delegation_valid_from`**, on any edge carrying `sub_delegation`, `license`, `grant`, `moderate`, `takedown`, `review` or `slash`, or sitting in an affiliation's `hierarchy` ([CC 4.4.3.2.8](part_4_composition_governance.md) C); a perpetual or over-ceiling edge is refused `delegation_term_required`; `delegation_valid_from` absent means the edge's own `asserted_at`, and `delegation_valid_until` absent on an edge that needs no term is open-ended, never malformed — `scope` is the [CC 2.1](#2.1) member (a bare token or a set; the one name for this wire member, never `delegated_scope[]`)

gist: delegation_valid_from absent means the edge's own asserted_at
entry_phrase: `delegation_valid_from` absent means the edge's own `asserted_at`, and `delegation_valid_until` absent on an edge that needs no term is open-ended, never malformed — `scope` is the [CC 2.1](#2.1) member (a bare token or a set; the one name for this wire member, never `delegated_scope[]`)

gist: delegation_valid_until absent on an edge that needs no term is open-ended, never malformed
entry_phrase: `delegation_valid_from` absent means the edge's own `asserted_at`, and `delegation_valid_until` absent on an edge that needs no term is open-ended, never malformed — `scope` is the [CC 2.1](#2.1) member (a bare token or a set; the one name for this wire member, never `delegated_scope[]`)

gist: the delegated scope rides the 2.1 scope member, a bare token or a set; never delegated_scope[]
entry_phrase: `delegation_valid_from` absent means the edge's own `asserted_at`, and `delegation_valid_until` absent on an edge that needs no term is open-ended, never malformed — `scope` is the [CC 2.1](#2.1) member (a bare token or a set; the one name for this wire member, never `delegated_scope[]`)

gist: supersedes replaces a prior row by the same attester; carries references_attestation_id, supersession_reason, differs_in[]
entry_phrase: | `supersedes` | This attestation row replaces a prior one by the same attester | `{references_attestation_id, supersession_reason, differs_in[]}` |

gist: withdraws retracts the signer's prior attestation without claiming it was false; carries references_attestation_id and withdrawal_reason
entry_phrase: A party [CC 2.4.1.1](#2.4.1.1) admits retracts a row (does NOT claim it was false)

gist: recants admits the signer's prior attestation was false at issuance; carries references_attestation_id, recantation_reason, what_was_false
entry_phrase: | `recants` | My prior attestation was false at issuance — admits epistemic error | `{references_attestation_id, recantation_reason, what_was_false}` |

gist: a doctrinal-development claim is supersedes with differs_in, not recants
entry_phrase: - A **doctrinal-development** claim ("this version extends but does not contradict the prior version") is `supersedes` with `differs_in: ["scope", "evidence_refs"]` — NOT `recants` (which would assert prior was false).

gist: an acknowledged-error claim is recants, distinct from withdraws
entry_phrase: - An **acknowledged-error** claim ("the prior framing was wrong; I admit the mistake") is `recants` — distinct from `withdraws` ([CC 2.4.1.1](#2.4.1.1)).

gist: a prudent retraction without a falsity claim is withdraws
entry_phrase: - A **prudent-retraction** ("I'm withdrawing without claiming it was false; context has changed") is `withdraws`.

gist: an authority-source claim is delegates_to with the authority key as attested_key_id, not a grounding:{tradition} prefix
entry_phrase: - An **authority-source claim via delegation** ("this constitutional position derives from authority-key X in scope Y") is `delegates_to` with X as `attested_key_id` (the [CC 2.4.1.2](#2.4.1.2) reuse pattern for authority-source claims, replacing what would otherwise need a `grounding:{tradition}:{principle}` prefix that fails [CC 1.2](part_1_foundation.md#1.2) T2).

gist: a framework claim names its source of authority by delegates_to against a framework key with scope naming the principle, not by a grounding prefix
entry_phrase: A constitutional or framework claim can name its source-of-authority by emitting `delegates_to` against an `attested_key_id` representing the framework, with `scope` naming the principle.

gist: a delegates_to with delegation_purpose owner_binding defines the self cohort; at most one is live per owned key and the substrate rejects a second distinct-owner binding at bind time
entry_phrase: **Owner-binding is the single-valued purpose.** A `delegates_to(user → node/agent)` carrying `delegation_purpose: owner_binding` is the owner-binding, held to the single-owner invariant ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md), *Who owns a key*).

gist: owner_binding is the one single-valued delegation_purpose; act-on-behalf, hierarchy and authority-source delegations are multi-parent DAGs
entry_phrase: This is the **one** `delegation_purpose` that is single-valued — act-on-behalf, hierarchy ([CC 4.5.13](part_4_composition_governance.md)), and authority-source delegations remain **multi-parent** DAGs.

gist: consumer policy may apply different trust adjustments to attesters who recant versus those who withdraw
entry_phrase: Consumer policy can apply different trust adjustments to attesters who `recant` versus those who `withdraw`.

gist: every claim about an entity, by any attester, is a scores attestation on a named dimension; scores is the one workhorse
entry_phrase: Every claim about an entity — positive or negative, identity or capability or behavior or state or commitment, by any attester source — is expressed as a `scores` attestation on a named dimension.

gist: the signed object is attestation_envelope with the row mirror and asserted_at; an optional member is omitted, never null
entry_phrase: Illustration of member placement, not canonical bytes: the signed object is `attestation_envelope` as [CC 2.6.1.7](#2.6.1.7) lays it out, with the `row` mirror and `asserted_at`, and an optional member is omitted, never null.

gist: a claim's validity in time is asserted_at plus optional valid_until, composed by the consumer with the substrate's expires_at
entry_phrase: `asserted_at` + optional `valid_until`; consumer composes with substrate `expires_at`

gist: reversibility is rollbackable or non-rollbackable, by consumer policy plus the per-prefix rule
entry_phrase: rollbackable / non-rollbackable (consumer policy + per-prefix rule)

gist: scope is one of self, family, community, affiliations, species, biosphere, federation
entry_phrase: self / family / community / affiliations / species / biosphere / federation

gist: The grammar has exactly five wire primitives: one workhorse and four composers; nothing more
entry_phrase: The grammar has exactly five wire-format primitives (one workhorse + four structural composers) and an open-vocabulary dimension namespace organized by mechanism-descriptive prefixes.

gist: Verdicts are composed by consumers under CC 4.4 policy; the wire format prescribes no verdict
entry_phrase: Consumers compose verdicts from primitive attestations using the policies in [CC 4.4](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4); nothing in the wire format prescribes what verdict to reach.

gist: Canonical bytes are computed over the literal envelope members the producer signs
entry_phrase: The canonical bytes are computed over **the literal envelope members the producer signs**.

gist: Optional fields the producer omits are never materialized into canonical bytes by any party
entry_phrase: Optional fields that the producer omits MUST NOT be materialized into canonical bytes by any party — producer, substrate, relay, or consumer.

gist: Optional fields the producer emits, even at default value, are preserved in canonical bytes by every party
entry_phrase: Optional fields that the producer explicitly emits (even at their default value) MUST be preserved in the canonical bytes by any party.

gist: Documented defaults apply at interpretation time, not encoding time
entry_phrase: Documented defaults from [CC 2.1](#2.1) are **interpretation-time semantics**, not encoding-time content.

gist: A consumer reads an absent epistemic_mode as direct; omitted and explicit-default encodings verify under their own bytes and are semantically equivalent
entry_phrase: **Both signatures verify under their respective canonical bytes.** Both are **semantically equivalent** — a CEG-Conforming Consumer evaluates `effective_epistemic_mode(envelope) = envelope.epistemic_mode if present else "direct"` and proceeds identically.

gist: A substrate, relay or consumer that re-stores or forwards a row preserves member presence and absence exactly as signed
entry_phrase: A substrate, relay, or consumer that re-stores or forwards an attestation MUST preserve member presence/absence exactly as the producer signed it:

gist: A relay never strips an explicitly emitted default member
entry_phrase: The canonical bytes are computed over **the literal envelope members the producer signs**. Optional fields that the producer omits MUST NOT be materialized into canonical bytes by any party — producer, substrate, relay, or consumer. Optional fields that the producer explicitly emits (even at their default value) MUST be preserved in the canonical bytes by any party. Documented defaults from [CC 2.1](#2.1) are **interpretation-time semantics**, not encoding-time content.

gist: A relay never materializes an omitted default member
entry_phrase: The canonical bytes are computed over **the literal envelope members the producer signs**. Optional fields that the producer omits MUST NOT be materialized into canonical bytes by any party — producer, substrate, relay, or consumer. Optional fields that the producer explicitly emits (even at their default value) MUST be preserved in the canonical bytes by any party. Documented defaults from [CC 2.1](#2.1) are **interpretation-time semantics**, not encoding-time content.

gist: A relay forwards canonical octets as received; one that re-serializes emits JCS member order and changes nothing else; presence and absence stay fixed
entry_phrase: A relay that re-serializes from a parsed object at all MUST emit JCS ([CC 2.6.1.3](#2.6.1.3)): canonical member order on re-emission is required, and nothing else changes — member presence/absence stays fixed

gist: Unknown fields are preserved on read and re-emission; the same preservation extends to known optional fields
entry_phrase: This composes with the [CC 2.1.1](#2.1.1) forward-compatibility rule (which already mandates preserving unknown fields on read and re-emission); the same preservation discipline extends to known-optional fields.

gist: Set-semantics array elements are sorted lexicographically by JCS string form (UTF-16 code-unit order) before signing
entry_phrase: - **Set-semantics** (order carries no meaning) — elements MUST be **lexicographically sorted by their JCS string form (UTF-16 code-unit order, ascending)** before signing.

gist: subject_key_ids[] and delegates_to.scope[] are set-semantics arrays and are sorted
entry_phrase: **`subject_key_ids[]` and `delegates_to.scope[]` are set-semantics → sorted.**

gist: transport_destination.aspects[], key_grant.rotation_chain and evidence_refs[] are sequence-semantics and keep authored order
entry_phrase: **`transport_destination.aspects[]`** (RNS hash preimage order), **`key_grant.rotation_chain`** (supersession lineage), and **`evidence_refs[]`** (producer-asserted order) are sequence-semantics → preserved.

gist: A field's definition declares set or sequence kind; absent a declaration the array is set-semantics (sorted)
entry_phrase: A field's definition MUST declare which kind it is; absent a declaration, set-semantics (sorted) is the default.

gist: A substrate refuses an out-of-order set array with federation_set_semantics_unsorted naming the member and never re-sorts it
entry_phrase: A substrate that finds a set-kind array out of order refuses the row with **`federation_set_semantics_unsorted`**, naming the member, and never re-sorts it (re-sorting would move signed bytes).

gist: A set-kind array is sorted and unique; a duplicate element is refused federation_set_semantics_unsorted
entry_phrase: **A set-kind array is sorted AND unique:** a duplicate element is refused under the same token.

gist: An optional member is unset by absence never null; explicit JSON null is refused federation_malformed_row reason envelope_member_null
entry_phrase: **An optional member is unset by absence, never by `null`:** an explicit JSON `null` on any optional envelope member is refused as malformed (the key plane's `revocation_envelope` of [CC 2.4.1.1](#2.4.1.1) is the one exception: it binds its absent optionals as explicit `null`) — a null and an absence would be two byte strings for one meaning, the duplicate rule again — refused as `federation_malformed_row` with reason `envelope_member_null` (one of the closed malformed-row reasons of [CC 2.6.1.7](#2.6.1.7), beside `envelope_member_missing` / `envelope_member_invalid`).

gist: The key plane revocation_envelope binds its absent optionals as explicit null (the one exception to the no-null rule)
entry_phrase: **An optional member is unset by absence, never by `null`:** an explicit JSON `null` on any optional envelope member is refused as malformed (the key plane's `revocation_envelope` of [CC 2.4.1.1](#2.4.1.1) is the one exception: it binds its absent optionals as explicit `null`) — a null and an absence would be two byte strings for one meaning, the duplicate rule again — refused as `federation_malformed_row` with reason `envelope_member_null` (one of the closed malformed-row reasons of [CC 2.6.1.7](#2.6.1.7), beside `envelope_member_missing` / `envelope_member_invalid`).

gist: Where this document writes a default as null it means absent
entry_phrase: Where this document writes a default as `null` it means *absent*.

gist: Every byte field's string encoding is pinned; hashes and raw key material (public keys, destination_hash, root_hash, digests, fingerprints) are lowercase hex, never base64 in canonical bytes
entry_phrase: **Hashes and raw key material — public keys, `destination_hash`, `root_hash`, digests and fingerprints — MUST be lowercase hex per [CC 2.6.3](#2.6.3)** (no `0x`, no separators, byte-length-exact; never base64 in canonical bytes).

gist: Fields explicitly documented as base64 use base64; the default for any key, hash or id byte field is lowercase hex
entry_phrase: Fields explicitly documented as base64 (e.g., `hardware_attestation`, an opaque attestation blob) use base64 as their definition states — but the *default* for any key/hash/id byte field is CC 2.6.3 lowercase hex.

gist: A subject_key_ids element naming a registered key carries the key_id string verbatim (label-fingerprint form or an older 64-hex id); the hex rule does not re-encode it
entry_phrase: - **`subject_key_ids[]` is the one two-form field, and [CC 2.3.2.1](#2.3.2.1) governs its second form.** An element naming a `federation_keys.key_id` — like `attesting_key_id` and `attested_key_id` — carries that key's `key_id` string **verbatim**: the [CC 2.6.8](#2.6.8) `<label>-<fingerprint>` form (lowercase `[a-z0-9-]`), or an older 64-hex id a directory still holds; a `key_id` is an identifier, not a byte field, so the hex rule above does not re-encode it.

gist: A canonical-hash subject element is the tagged canonical:{hashalg}:{hex} string; the untagged bare-hex spelling is refused at the gate
entry_phrase: An element naming a canonical-hash subject is the **tagged** `canonical:{hashalg}:{hex}` string, which CC 2.3.2.1 REQUIRES and whose untagged bare-hex spelling CC 2.3.2.1 refuses at the gate.

gist: The canonical: prefix is a tagged-union discriminator exempt from the no-separators hex rule; only the {hex} segment is governed by 2.6.3
entry_phrase: The CC 2.6.3 hex rule governs the `{hex}` segment of that string only; the `canonical:{hashalg}:` prefix is a tagged-union discriminator, outside CC 2.6.3's scope and **exempt from the no-separators rule**.

gist: Every base64 field uses the RFC 4648 section 4 standard alphabet, with padding, no whitespace or newlines
entry_phrase: - **The base64 variant is pinned: every field documented as base64 MUST use the RFC 4648 §4 STANDARD alphabet, WITH padding, no whitespace or embedded newlines**.

gist: The vector set includes a base64-variant round-trip case across two independent encoders
entry_phrase: The vector set MUST include a base64-variant case (encode→sign→verify round-trip across two independent encoders).

gist: Every datetime field is the 2.6.2 canonical string: UTC literal Z, exactly three fractional digits
entry_phrase: **Timestamp encoding.** Every datetime field (`signed_at`, `asserted_at`, `valid_until`, `delegation_valid_from`/`_until`, `valid_at`, …) is the **[CC 2.6.2](#2.6.2) canonical string** — UTC literal `Z` (never `+00:00`), millisecond precision (exactly three fractional digits), `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`.

gist: The cross-implementation JCS vector set covers a set-vs-sequence array case, a hex-vs-base64 byte case and a timestamp case
entry_phrase: The cross-impl JCS vector set MUST cover all three (a set-vs-sequence array case, a hex-vs-base64 byte case, a timestamp case) alongside the per-Contribution vectors.

gist: The omit-vs-materialize rule applies uniformly to every optional CC 2.1 envelope field
entry_phrase: The omit-vs-materialize rule applies uniformly to every optional [CC 2.1](#2.1) field.

gist: row.subject_key_ids is always present in the mirror ([] when no subject); the column beside the row is absent when empty
entry_phrase: always present in the mirror, `[]` when there is no subject; the `subject_key_ids` column beside the row is absent when empty

gist: session_id and claimed_at are required on session:* rows
entry_phrase: n/a (REQUIRED on `session:*`)

gist: custody_state is required on a custody report; admission refuses one without it
entry_phrase: | `custody_state` | CC 3.1.3.3 | n/a (REQUIRED on a custody report) | member absent (not a custody report; on one, admission refuses) | `"custody_state":"none"` |

gist: group_kind and expires_at are required on a membership proposal; admission refuses one without them
entry_phrase: | `group_kind` | CC 3.1.3.2 | n/a (REQUIRED on a membership proposal) | member absent (not a proposal; on one, admission refuses) | `"group_kind":"family"` |

gist: proposal_hash is required on a membership answer; admission refuses one without it
entry_phrase: | `proposal_hash` | CC 3.1.3.2 | n/a (REQUIRED on a membership answer) | member absent (not an answer; on one, admission refuses) | `"proposal_hash":"<original_content_hash>"` |

gist: attached_head_digest is required on a new trust:accepts:v1 edge; one without it is refused; an edge admitted before the requirement stays valid
entry_phrase: | `attached_head_digest` | CC 3.2 T4a | n/a (REQUIRED on `trust:accepts:v1`) | member absent (not an acceptance edge; a NEW acceptance edge without it is refused; an edge admitted before the member was required stays valid, T4) | `"attached_head_digest":"<64-char-lowercase>"` |

gist: attach_window_secs absent means no attach window; attach by out-of-band anchor only
entry_phrase: absent = no window declared (attach by out-of-band anchor only)

gist: witness_cadence_secs, witness_quorum and witnesses are required on a witnessed lineage's charter; absent, the lineage is unwitnessed for T6
entry_phrase: | `witness_cadence_secs` | CC 3.2 T6 | n/a (REQUIRED on a witnessed lineage's charter) | member absent (the lineage is unwitnessed for T6) | `"witness_cadence_secs":86400` |

gist: halt_fuse_secs defaults to the constant 86400 when absent; an explicit value overrides
entry_phrase: | `halt_fuse_secs` | CC 4.2.1.1 | **86400** — a constitutional constant, not a substrate default | member absent ≡ `86400` (a verifier reads the constant) | `"halt_fuse_secs":3600` (an explicit value overrides) |

gist: recovery_commitments is required on the accord's charter; absent, no holder can self-rotate and recovery is a roster change
entry_phrase: | `recovery_commitments` | CC 4.2.6 | n/a (REQUIRED on the accord's charter) | member absent (no holder can self-rotate; recovery is a roster change) | `"recovery_commitments":{"<holder_key_id>":"<64 lowercase hex>"}` |

gist: family_id is required iff cohort_scope is family; admission rejects a family-scoped row without it
entry_phrase: | `family_id` | CC 3.3.4 | n/a (REQUIRED iff `cohort_scope == family`) | member absent (admission rejects if cohort_scope == family) | `"family_id":"..."` |

gist: community_id is required iff cohort_scope is community or affiliations; admission rejects such a row without it
entry_phrase: | `community_id` | CC 3.2 | n/a (REQUIRED iff `cohort_scope ∈ {community, affiliations}`) | member absent (admission rejects if `cohort_scope ∈ {community, affiliations}`) | `"community_id":"..."` |

gist: delivery_mode defaults to pull and history_on_join to from_join when absent
entry_phrase: | `delivery_mode` | CC 5.3.3 | `pull` | member absent | `"delivery_mode":"push"` |

gist: family_id and community_id are conditional-required, not optional-with-default; the substrate rejects a mis-shaped row
entry_phrase: The conditional-required fields `family_id` and `community_id` are NOT optional-with-default ([CC 2.1.1](#2.1.1)), but they encode under the same JCS rule when present.

gist: A relay preserves member presence and absence exactly and forwards as-received bytes; defaults are applied after signature verification
entry_phrase: > Bob's relay MUST preserve member presence/absence exactly ([CC 2.6.1.1](#2.6.1.1)). Bob forwards the as-received bytes. Carol's verify succeeds. The semantic interpretation step at Carol (applying default `"direct"` to the absent member) happens AFTER signature verification.

gist: A signature is verified over JCS(envelope) by the hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 path

gist: cosign state is closed to pending and signature; a pending row carries the event whole less its cosignatures, its primary signer and the primary's signature.
entry_phrase: **The collection of cosignatures for an event its protocol has not yet admitted** (registered under CC 3.1.7 R2(a); the hold of [CC 3.3.4](part_3_the_namespace.md), general to any cosigned row of [CC 2.4](part_2_the_grammar.md)): `{state}` ∈ `pending` \| `signature` — closed; wire `cosign:pending:v1`, `cosign:signature:v1`. A **pending** row carries a cosignable event whole, as its typed door takes it, less its cosignatures: the event, its primary signer and, as its own statement, the primary's signature over the event's signing bytes. It is named by the event's **quorum key**, sha256(`ciris-persist/cosign-pending/v1` ‖ JCS(the event with no signature in it)): the digest of what every signer signs, covering no signature, so it is equal on every node whatever signature bytes that node holds. It is admitted only if the primary's signature verifies and the primary resolves to an active member of the group at the event's signed instant. That instant is the signer's to choose, so it is bounded as [CC 3.3.6.3](#3.3.6.3) bounds an owner act: a pending row whose primary is no longer an active member at receipt is refused `asserted_at_stale` once its signed instant is older than the freshness window W ([CC 2.6.7](part_2_the_grammar.md)). It is the ruling [CC 4.3](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.3) publishes on the accountability cadence and composes into the WA's conduct record; it is not a `wa_adjudication` finding, which is a quorum's decision about seats. The wire shape of the response is the substrate's. Reserved to a seated key.

entry_phrase: It is **advertised over the existing `federation_session` / `key_grant` entitlement surface — NOT a new wire** — and the sender drops chunks above the cap without re-encoding.

gist: admits(layer) is the per-axis test spatial, temporal and quality each at most the policy cap; a codec_id 0xFF chunk MUST be admitted unconditionally before consulting admits

entry_phrase: A live stream is its own transparency log, which is what makes a producer accountable for what it streamed: the signed roots commit the producer to a single chunk history.

gist: log_id is the string stream:<stream_id>; chunks are leaves; the stream-root is a SignedTreeHead with that log_id, tree_size = chunk_count, root_hash, timestamp, signature
entry_phrase: - `log_id = "stream:<stream_id>"` — the bare `stream_id` is the stream's logical identity; the log identifier as signed and served is the string `stream:<stream_id>`; chunks = leaves; stream-root = `SignedTreeHead{ log_id: "stream:<stream_id>", tree_size: chunk_count, root_hash, timestamp, signature }`.

gist: A live stream produces signed roots at the cadence whether or not anyone records it
entry_phrase: **A live stream produces these at the cadence below whether or not anyone records it**.

gist: The producer MUST sign the stream STH; signing bytes with no domain label, little-endian: u32 len(log_id) || log_id || u64 tree_size || root_hash[32] || i64 timestamp seconds || u32 nanoseconds

gist: root_hash is the RFC 6962 Merkle root over the first tree_size chunk SHA-256 leaves in seq order, leaves under 0x00 and inner nodes under 0x01

entry_phrase: An inline file is a stream of one leaf: `stream_id` is the inline blob's stream id and `tree_size` is 1.

gist: Witness cosign of a stream root is optional: best-effort open media uses the producer-signed root only; accountable streams (paid, registry propagation, emergency) take witness cosign with consistency proof
entry_phrase: - **Accountable** (paid media, registry propagation, emergency) → witness cosign per [CC 5.3.1.1](#5.3.1.1) consistency-proof, which is the **anti-equivocation guarantee** — producer cannot show different chunk-K to different subscribers nor rewrite mid-stream

gist: The producer publishes a signed root every K chunks or T seconds, always at an epoch boundary and at sealed_at; witness cosign runs per epoch; defaults K=64, T=2s, operator-tunable
entry_phrase: - **Cadence**: producer publishes a signed root every `K` chunks OR `T` seconds (whichever first), **always at an epoch boundary** (CC 5.1) + at `sealed_at`. Witness cosign runs **per-epoch** (coarser than per-K to keep cosign-quorum cost off the hot path). Default pins: **K=64, T=2s** (operator-tunable)

gist: A subscriber verifies chunk K's inclusion against the nearest signed STH at or past K via the consistency path; no new commitment structure
entry_phrase: - **Incremental verify**: each leaf's "root-after-K" lets a subscriber verify chunk K's inclusion against the nearest signed STH ≥ K via the [CC 5.3.1.1](#5.3.1.1) consistency path.

gist: The accountable-stream witness quorum is Policy E locality-scaled, not a fixed N
entry_phrase: - **Accountable-stream quorum**: Policy E ([CC 4.4.3.1](part_4_composition_governance.md) locality-scaled quorum) applies — not a fixed N.

gist: A live_stream is its own per-stream log instance and MUST NOT append chunks into the federation provenance log
entry_phrase: A `live_stream` MUST NOT append chunks into the federation provenance log ([CC 5.3.1](#5.3.1)'s global log carrying builds / licenses / identities) — millions of media chunks would pollute provenance and inflate the global tree.

gist: The streaming path reuses the 5.3.1 SignedTreeHead, ConsistencyProof, WitnessConsistencyProof and cosign abstractions per stream under the same RFC 6962 algorithm
entry_phrase: The CC 5.3.3 path **reuses** the CC 5.3.1 `SignedTreeHead` / `ConsistencyProof` / `WitnessConsistencyProof` / cosign abstractions, instantiated per-stream as separate log instances under the same RFC 6962 algorithm.

gist: No new attestation_type values: chunks ride content addressing, stream-roots ride SignedTreeHead, delivery receipts ride scores against the delivery_receipt:{stream_id} reserved prefix
entry_phrase: Stream chunks ride content addressing; stream-roots ride the existing `SignedTreeHead` shape; delivery receipts ride `scores` against the new `delivery_receipt:{stream_id}` reserved prefix ([CC 3.4.6](part_3_the_namespace.md)).

entry_phrase: - **Leaf order MUST be lexicographic** over leaf bytes (the [CC 2.6.1.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) set-semantics rule). Any "either order as long as both peers agree" convention is **non-conformant** — it is the CC 2.6.1-class divergence hazard.

gist: Merkle scheme: leaf = SHA-256(leaf_bytes), node = SHA-256(left,right), odd-node duplication, empty sentinel b"WW-v1-empty"; no RFC 6962 leaf/node prefix

gist: The leaf list is deduplicated as well as sorted; a list with a repeated leaf is refused before hashing
entry_phrase: **CEG does NOT adopt the RFC 6962 `0x00`/`0x01` leaf/node prefix here.** Rationale: the odd-node-duplication malleability is **not exploitable in this construction's uses, given one rule: the leaf list MUST be deduplicated as well as sorted — the [CC 2.6.1.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) set rule, sorted AND unique — and a list with a repeated leaf is refused before hashing.** (A repeated id in `sources` is refused at descent and in the aggregate builder as `federation_malformed_row` / `aggregate_source_duplicate`, so `source_count` and `n_eff` always count distinct ids.) Without that rule the lists `[a,b,c]` and `[a,b,c,c]` share a root under odd-node duplication and neither signing nor full-list recomputation tells them apart; with it, the duplicated list is never a valid input, and the remaining uses are safe because (1) every wholeness witness and `member_commitment` ([CC 6.1.2.1.1](#6.1.2.1.1)) root is **mandatorily hybrid-signed** — no consumer ever relies on an *unsigned* root; (2) `member_commitment` is verified by **recomputation from the full source-id list**, never by partial inclusion proofs against the bare root (malleability moot); (3) the CC 6.1.1 reconciliation Merkle-proof exchange (N4) is between **accountable, signed, equivocation-checked peers** — not third-party forgery of an untrusted root.

gist: The wholeness-witness Merkle scheme and the 5.3.1 RFC 6962 log are distinct constructions and must not be cross-verified; changing the scheme is a vector-invalidating wire change

gist: N3: a wholeness witness is a federation-tier attestation, hybrid-PQC verified at ingest and before persistence to the witness corpus
entry_phrase: - **N3** — a wholeness witness is a federation-tier attestation: hybrid PQC verified at ingest **and before** persistence to the witness corpus ([CC 6.1.3](#6.1.3)); `compare_witnesses` MUST NOT run on an unverified witness.

gist: compare_witnesses never runs on an unverified witness
entry_phrase: - **N3** — a wholeness witness is a federation-tier attestation: hybrid PQC verified at ingest **and before** persistence to the witness corpus ([CC 6.1.3](#6.1.3)); `compare_witnesses` MUST NOT run on an unverified witness.

gist: N4: two validly signed witnesses from the same (peer_id, epoch_id, claim_namespace_set) with different roots are non-repudiable equivocation; the substrate retains and surfaces them as a hard_case row, never silently reconciles
entry_phrase: - **N4 (equivocation)** — two validly-signed witnesses from the same `(peer_id, epoch_id, claim_namespace_set)` with different `merkle_root` are **non-repudiable equivocation proof**; the substrate MUST retain and surface them as a `hard_case:{kind}` row (the registered open vocabulary of [CC 3.1.9.4](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.9.4)), never silently reconcile.

gist: Per-peer epoch_id is anti-rollback-checked before EpochBehind is used as a reconciliation input
entry_phrase: Per-peer `epoch_id` MUST be anti-rollback-checked before `EpochBehind` is used as a reconciliation input (eclipse guard).

gist: Full cross-witness BFT may be deferred but observed equivocation is never discarded
entry_phrase: Full cross-witness BFT MAY be deferred ([CC 8.3](part_8_appendices.md)) — but observed equivocation MUST NOT be discarded.

gist: A wholeness witness only triggers the quorum-merge; it never decides a merge and never replaces monotonic_quorum or revision anti-rollback for revocation, partner_record or org_membership
entry_phrase: - **WW vs replication (the highest-value reconciliation)** — a wholeness witness is a **divergence detector that *triggers*** the [CC 5.3.2.3](part_5_transport_substrate.md) quorum-merge; it does **NOT** decide a merge and MUST NOT replace `monotonic_quorum` / `revision` anti-rollback for `revocation` / `partner_record` / `org_membership`.

gist: A Divergent verdict on revocation, partner_record or org_membership hands the decision to the quorum-merge so recover-from-any-holder cannot resurrect a revoked key
entry_phrase: A `Divergent` verdict on those subject_kinds hands the decision to the CC 5.3.2.3 quorum-merge (quorum-ordered, anti-rollback) — otherwise a "recover from any holder" path could resurrect a revoked key (rollback).

gist: AggregationMetaV1 is CEG-canonical: this section defines its byte layout and implementations conform to it; reference implementations store it opaque
entry_phrase: This shape is **CEG-canonical** — the reference implementations store `aggregation_meta` **opaque**, so a change in one never forces a change in the other, and this section **defines** the byte layout and implementations conform to it.

gist: AggregationMetaV1 is a substrate wire shape, not a 2.1 attestation; its preimage uses the 6.1.3 binary discipline, not JCS
entry_phrase: `AggregationMetaV1` is a **substrate wire shape, NOT a [CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) attestation** — no 1+4 change. Its signing preimage uses the [CC 6.1.3](#6.1.3) binary discipline (length-prefixed, big-endian, domain-separated — **NOT** [CC 2.6.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) JCS). Preimage byte order (normative):

gist: AggregationMetaV1 preimage order: 16-byte separator AGG-META-v1, u32 version=3, content_id, corpus_kind, u32 tier, algorithm id, u32 source_count, member_commitment[32], noise_floor_descriptor, u32 n_eff, u32 max_source_multiplicity, mass_commitment[32]
entry_phrase: preimage = b"AGG-META-v1\0\0\0\0\0" // 16-byte domain separator (exact)

gist: The domain separator is the same for every version; layouts are discriminated by the version field alone; re-ordering is a vector-invalidating wire change
entry_phrase: The layout above is the complete preimage. The domain separator is the same for every `version` value, so discrimination between layouts is carried by the `version` field alone. This byte order is golden-vectored (`aggregation_meta/canonical_bytes_v3`) and reproduced cross-impl; re-ordering it is a vector-invalidating wire change.

gist: version = 3 is the only admissible AggregationMetaV1 value with no deprecation window; a verifier rejects version below 3; both admission gates fail closed on a lower version
entry_phrase: **Version (normative).** `version = 3` is the only admissible value, with **no deprecation window**: a verifier MUST reject a tier at `version < 3` as inadmissible. Both [CC 6.1.2.1.2](#6.1.2.1.2) admission gates — the R9 multiplicity gate over `max_source_multiplicity` and the mass-dominance gate over the signed `n_eff` — read members only this layout carries, and both fail **closed** on a lower version.

gist: content_id, byte ids and commitments render as lowercase hex; on the wire commitments are raw 32 bytes
entry_phrase: `content_id`, byte-valued ids, `member_commitment` and `mass_commitment` are lowercase-hex per [CC 2.6.3](part_2_the_grammar.md) where rendered as strings; both commitments on the wire are the raw 32 bytes.

gist: Bound-hybrid signature Ed25519(preimage) plus ML-DSA-65(preimage,ed25519_sig); a verifier rejects a tier lacking a valid ML-DSA-65 half at ingest and before persistence
entry_phrase: **Bound-hybrid signature** (the [CC 6.1.3](#6.1.3) rule): `Ed25519(preimage)` + `ML-DSA-65(preimage ‖ ed25519_sig)`; a verifier MUST reject a tier lacking a valid ML-DSA-65 half **at ingest and before persistence** (the [CC 5.3.2.4.3.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md) store-path rule applies — `AggregationMetaV1` is federation-tier).

gist: Replication is bounded by wire type, membership (cohort_scope) and consent:replication; the owner storage bound is a declared CEG rule, not per-node implementation choice, because the substrate never invents replication policy
entry_phrase: Because the substrate MUST NOT invent replication policy ([CC 5.3.2.3](part_5_transport_substrate.md)), this bound is a **declared CEG rule**, not implementation-defined per node.

gist: B1: identity, consent and config records are always pinned and exempt from the byte budget; corpus is pin-on-consent, cache otherwise
entry_phrase: - **B1 (pin classes).** Identity, consent, and config records are **always pinned** — small, identity-critical, durable, and **exempt from the byte budget**.

gist: B2: a corpus content_id is pinned iff an active consent:replication grant authorizes its subject_kind (the grant is the pin authorization) and the owner lists that class in its StorageBudgetV1
entry_phrase: - **B2 (pin-on-consent).** A corpus `content_id` is **pinned** (durable) iff **both** hold: (i) an active `consent:replication` grant ([CC 3.3.7](part_3_the_namespace.md)) authorizes the corpus `subject_kind` covering it — the grant **is** the pin authorization (no separate pin dimension); a `consent:replication` grant names corpus `subject_kind`s in its authorized-class list, extending its attestation-prefix grammar to the corpus track of [CC 5.3.2.3](part_5_transport_substrate.md); **and** (ii) the owner **elects** to spend budget on that class by listing it in the `pinned_class` set of its `StorageBudgetV1` (B3).

gist: Corpus received without a satisfied pin is cache: eviction-eligible and descends before any pinned content under pressure
entry_phrase: Corpus received without a satisfied pin is **cache**: eviction-eligible, and it descends **before** any pinned content under pressure ([CC 6.1.2.3](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md)).

gist: B3: a StorageBudgetV1 allots per cohort_scope a budget_bytes ceiling and a pin_reserve_bytes floor at most budget_bytes; pinned corpus fits its budget; excess is refused or descends first
entry_phrase: - **B3 (owner budget — per `cohort_scope`).** An owner declares a `StorageBudgetV1` (below) allotting, **per `cohort_scope`**, a `budget_bytes` ceiling and a `pin_reserve_bytes` floor (MUST be `≤ budget_bytes`) held for pinned corpus.

gist: A StorageBudgetV1 inherits the self/family suppression: self and family entries never appear in a signed or federated budget; those budgets are enforced locally only
entry_phrase: A `StorageBudgetV1` **inherits the [CC 5.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md) `self | family` suppression**: `self` and `family` scope entries MUST NOT appear in a signed / federated budget — those budgets are enforced **locally only**, else the budget would leak the existence of structurally-invisible content (the same hazard the [CC 5.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md#5.2) audience rule closes for holding claims).

gist: Budgets supersede by monotonic revision: a higher revision from the same node_id supersedes and a lower one is rejected (anti-rollback)
entry_phrase: Budgets are **supersedable** by monotonic `revision` — the **anti-rollback** aspect of [CC 5.3.2.3](part_5_transport_substrate.md) (a single-owner self-declaration, not a multi-signer quorum): a higher `revision` from the same `node_id` supersedes; a lower one MUST be rejected.

gist: B4: large corpus is wanted-then-pulled, never unsolicited-pushed; a producer never pushes an object exceeding the receiver's advertised size_cap
entry_phrase: - **B4 (want/have + size cap).** Large corpus is **wanted-then-pulled**, never unsolicited-pushed: a peer advertises a `want` for content **within its remaining scope budget** and a `size_cap`; a producer MUST NOT push a corpus object exceeding the receiver's advertised `size_cap`.

gist: Content is content-addressed: a content_id pinned by several scopes occupies its bytes once and is retained while any scope pins it
entry_phrase: Content is content-addressed (CID-style): a pin is a stable reference and dedup is free — a `content_id` pinned by several scopes occupies its bytes **once** and is retained while **any** scope pins it.

gist: B5: over budget under disk pressure the descent order is deterministic: cache before pinned; within pinned lowest rarity first; ties by oldest revision
entry_phrase: - **B5 (contention arbitration).** When a scope is over budget under disk pressure, descent order ([CC 6.1.2.3](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md)) is deterministic: **cache before pinned**; within pinned, **lowest rarity ([CC 6.1.5](#6.1.5)) first**; ties broken by **oldest `revision`**.

gist: A StorageBudgetV1 is consumption-challengeable: declared consumption is reconcilable against the pinned content_ids actually held; per-scope consumption accounting is edge-internal, never trusted from the wire
entry_phrase: A `StorageBudgetV1` is **consumption-challengeable** the way [CC 6.1.5](#6.1.5) N6 makes holding claims challengeable — an owner's declared consumption MUST be reconcilable against the pinned `content_id`s it actually holds, so a forged budget cannot become a force-evict channel against a competitor's content.

gist: B6: pinning never defeats consent; an active withdraws or consent:state:revoked forces immediate descent below the floor regardless of pin; a pin holds only against capacity pressure
entry_phrase: - **B6 (consent supremacy preserved).** Pinning **never** defeats consent: an active `withdraws` / `consent:state:revoked` still forces immediate descent below the noise floor regardless of pin state ([CC 6.1.5](#6.1.5) N5).

gist: StorageBudgetV1 is substrate framing, not a 2.1 attestation; its preimage uses the 6.1.3 binary discipline, not JCS
entry_phrase: **`StorageBudgetV1` — the owner's per-`cohort_scope` allotment (normative wire shape).** A substrate-framing object, **not** a [CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) attestation — no 1+4 change. Its signing preimage uses the [CC 6.1.3](#6.1.3) binary discipline (length-prefixed, big-endian, domain-separated — **NOT** [CC 2.6.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) JCS):

gist: StorageBudgetV1 preimage: separator CIRIS-STG-BUDGET, u32 version=1, node_id, epoch_id, u64 revision, u32 scope_count, per scope (cohort_scope, u64 budget_bytes, u64 pin_reserve_bytes), u32 pinned_class_count, subject_kinds; lists sorted and deduplicated
entry_phrase: preimage = b"CIRIS-STG-BUDGET"                 // 16-byte domain separator (exact)

gist: A StorageBudgetV1 is bound-hybrid signed; a verifier rejects one lacking a valid ML-DSA-65 half at ingest and before persistence
entry_phrase: **Bound-hybrid signature** (the [CC 6.1.3](#6.1.3) rule): `Ed25519(preimage)` + `ML-DSA-65(preimage ‖ ed25519_sig)`; a verifier MUST reject a `StorageBudgetV1` lacking a valid ML-DSA-65 half **at ingest and before persistence** (the [CC 5.3.2.4.3.1](part_5_transport_substrate.md) store-path rule — `StorageBudgetV1` is federation-tier).

gist: A higher revision from the same node_id supersedes; a lower one is rejected
entry_phrase: A higher `revision` from the same `node_id` supersedes; a lower one MUST be rejected (anti-rollback).

gist: A verifier rejects a StorageBudgetV1 if any pin_reserve_bytes exceeds budget_bytes, if scope or subject_kind lists are not sorted and deduplicated, or if a self or family scope entry is present
entry_phrase: **Validation (normative).** A verifier MUST **reject** a `StorageBudgetV1` if any `pin_reserve_bytes > budget_bytes`; if the `cohort_scope` entries or any `subject_kind` list are not lexicographically sorted and deduplicated; or if a `self` / `family` scope entry is present (B3 suppression).

gist: Two StorageBudgetV1 from the same (node_id, revision) with differing content are equivocation: a peer retains and surfaces both as hard_case and never silently picks one
entry_phrase: Two `StorageBudgetV1` from the same `(node_id, revision)` with differing content are **equivocation**: a peer MUST retain and surface both as a `hard_case:*` ([CC 3.1.9.4](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.9.4)) and MUST NOT silently pick one — mirroring the [CC 6.1.1](#6.1.1) N4 rule.

gist: CorpusWantV1 advertises exactly what corpus a peer will accept and its per-object ceiling; a producer pulls only against it
entry_phrase: **`CorpusWantV1` — the B4 want/have advertisement (normative wire shape).** A peer advertises exactly what corpus it will accept and its per-object ceiling; a producer pulls only against it.

gist: CorpusWantV1 preimage: separator CIRIS-WANT-HAVE plus NUL, u32 version=1, node_id, epoch_id, cohort_scope, u64 size_cap_bytes, u64 remaining_budget_bytes, u32 want_count, content_ids sorted and deduplicated
entry_phrase: preimage = b"CIRIS-WANT-HAVE\0"                // 16-byte domain separator (exact; one trailing NUL)

gist: A producer never pushes a corpus object exceeding the advertised size_cap_bytes nor one whose content_id is absent from an active CorpusWantV1 from the receiver
entry_phrase: A producer MUST NOT push a corpus object whose size exceeds the advertised `size_cap_bytes`, nor any object whose `content_id` is absent from an active `CorpusWantV1` from the receiver (**wanted-then-pulled, never unsolicited-pushed**).

gist: A CorpusWantV1 never names a self or family cohort_scope
entry_phrase: A `CorpusWantV1` MUST NOT name a `self` / `family` `cohort_scope`.

gist: PIN line: StorageBudgetV1 and CorpusWantV1 preimages are pin-normative with all lists sorted over UTF-8 bytes and deduplicated before signing; consumption accounting is edge-internal
entry_phrase: **PIN line.** `StorageBudgetV1` and `CorpusWantV1` signed preimages = **PIN-NORMATIVE** (all `cohort_scope`, `subject_kind`, and `content_id` lists sorted lexicographically over UTF-8 bytes and deduplicated before signing); per-scope **consumption accounting = edge-internal** (recomputed from held content per B5, never on the wire).

gist: The economic who-pays dimension is off-wire (billing) and not part of the storage shapes
entry_phrase: *Scope.* This section supplies the **technical** storage bound (quota + budget + pin); the **economic** *who-pays* dimension is deliberately off-wire ([CC 3.3.9](part_3_the_namespace.md) billing) and is not part of these shapes.

gist: recursive_trust_bootstrap walks a signed witness chain to a root in the peer's own trust graph; it is reachability discovery, not an admission shortcut
entry_phrase: `recursive_trust_bootstrap(SignedClaim, TrustGraph, WitnessChain) → verdict` lets a peer discover transitive trust by walking a signed witness chain to a root in its own trust graph. **It is reachability discovery beneath CEG's authority layer, not an admission shortcut** — discovering that you *can* reach someone is held strictly distinct from being *admitted* among them (Justice).

gist: N1: a chain walk yields trust-plus-serve standing only; admission to a non-infrastructure community stays gated at the destination by steward binding and the community's consensus_protocol
entry_phrase: - **N1 (trust ≠ membership)** — a successful chain walk yields **trust+serve standing only** ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md) TRUST≠MEMBERSHIP). Admission to any **non-`infrastructure`** community remains gated, at the destination, by (a) the CC 3.2 **steward-binding** precondition (exactly one live owner-binding `delegates_to` from a `user`-role identity; an `identity_occurrence` binds nothing) and (b) that community's `consensus_protocol`. `infrastructure` roots stay **founder-quorum**-gated; a transitive chain MUST NOT satisfy founder-quorum. `SignedClaim` carries the steward-binding fields so the gate is expressible.

gist: infrastructure roots stay founder-quorum gated; a transitive chain never satisfies founder quorum; SignedClaim carries steward-binding fields
entry_phrase: - **N1 (trust ≠ membership)** — a successful chain walk yields **trust+serve standing only** ([CC 3.2](part_3_the_namespace.md) TRUST≠MEMBERSHIP). Admission to any **non-`infrastructure`** community remains gated, at the destination, by (a) the CC 3.2 **steward-binding** precondition (exactly one live owner-binding `delegates_to` from a `user`-role identity; an `identity_occurrence` binds nothing) and (b) that community's `consensus_protocol`. `infrastructure` roots stay **founder-quorum**-gated; a transitive chain MUST NOT satisfy founder-quorum. `SignedClaim` carries the steward-binding fields so the gate is expressible.

gist: N2: chain length is at most the 5-hop cap, trust-graph cycles are rejected, the aggregate-weight cap (default 0.5 times root_trust) bounds transitive standing; a supplied chain proves only its signatures
entry_phrase: - **N2 (self-supplied chains aren't evidence)** — the chain-length budget MUST be ≤ the [CC 4.1.1](part_4_composition_governance.md) **5-hop cap**, trust-graph **cycles MUST be rejected** (CC 4.1.1), and the CC 4.1.1 **aggregate-weight cap** (default 0.5 × root_trust) MUST bound the standing one root confers transitively.

gist: RB-1: anonymous-tier content is ingestible, retainable and serveable with no trust-graph position; recursive_trust_bootstrap is never required for or invoked on anonymous records
entry_phrase: - **RB-1 (anonymous coexistence)** — anonymous-tier content MUST be ingestible / retainable / serveable with **no trust-graph position**; `recursive_trust_bootstrap` MUST NOT be required for, or invoked on, anonymous records.

For `safety_battery`, `{kind}` ∈ `capture` \| `interpret`: a **capture** is the question-and-answer pairs for one `{cell}` (a language and a domain, as `ru_mental_health`) against one agent version and one model, with its CI provenance; an **interpret** is a judge's per-criterion verdicts over the capture of the same `{prefix}`, the blob citing the rubric's id, version and hash and the judge model and prompt hash. gist: observation:reachability is one scores row per target per change-or-heartbeat; observed is a label not a key; endpoint or via names what was hit; score +1/0/-1 plus latency, confidence, evidence, valid_until.
entry_phrase: **A first-person probe result: "from here, at this instant, a request to this target answered, or did not."** The monitoring node (ciris-status) signs one `scores` row per observed target per change-or-heartbeat: `observed` names the target by a stable id (`service:us.billing`, `provider:groq`) — a label, **not** a federation key, since most targets have none; `endpoint` or `via` say what was actually hit; `score` is `operational` / `degraded` / `outage` → `+1` / `0` / `−1`; `latency_ms`, `confidence`, `evidence_refs[]` and `valid_until` carry the measurement. The subject of the row is the **observation**, which is the signer's own: `attesting_key_id` = `attested_key_id`, `witness_relation: self`, `subject_key_ids` empty, and the signer's key **is** the vantage. It is deliberately not `health:liveness`: that row says a keyed service *is alive*, which one vantage cannot know; this one says what one vantage *saw*, and a reader composes several vantages' observations into its own view of liveness. It is also not `peer_reachability:{network}` ([CC 3.1.4](part_3_the_namespace.md)), which is an edge's substrate self-report about its own transport peers. An observer of reachability is **not** thereby a lineage witness ([CC 3.4.10](part_3_the_namespace.md)): hosting both on one node is permitted, and neither role confers the other. The `observation:` stem is closed to this leaf and `observation:access_assumption:v1` below. **First-person:** `attesting_key_id` = `attested_key_id`; `witness_relation: self`; never emitted about, or on behalf of, another key

gist: access_assumption has score fixed +1, subject_key_ids REQUIRED non-empty naming the observed agent, members consent_basis, trace_level, occurrence_key_ids, window fields, channel_classes, and evidence_refs naming grants and traces relied on.
entry_phrase: **What one witness assumed about its view of a subject when it made a claim about that subject: which consent grants were in force, at what trace level, over which occurrences, over which window, through which channel classes**. A first-person observation, the same shape as `observation:reachability`: `attesting_key_id` = `attested_key_id` = the witness, `witness_relation: self`, `score` fixed at `+1` (the observation was made; positive only). Unlike reachability, the observed party has keys, so `subject_key_ids` is **REQUIRED and non-empty**: the observed agent's key or keys. Members ([CC 2.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)): `consent_basis` (the grants relied on), `trace_level`, `occurrence_key_ids`, `window`, `window_from`, `window_to`, `channel_classes`; `evidence_refs[]` names the `consent:state:granted` rows relied on and the trace rows or their window digest; `valid_until`. Any witness that emits a claim about a subject MAY emit one; LensCore emits one per (subject, scoring window) beside its `capacity:*` rows. It is never emitted by the subject about itself ([CC 3.4.5](#3.4.5)). Admission: every grant `consent_basis` cites MUST be live at the row's `asserted_at`, as for the claim it accompanies. Why it exists: two capacity rows with the same score, one computed from full traces and one from generic-level traces, are otherwise indistinguishable, and a composite over factor rows has no way to tell whether they saw the same interface. **First-person:** `attesting_key_id` = `attested_key_id`; `witness_relation: self`; `subject_key_ids` non-empty, naming the observed agent; never emitted by the subject

gist: A watchlist is enabled or disabled by the moderate or takedown authority of the group they moderate, signed, and revocable by withdraws.
entry_phrase: **Per-group content-watchlist config**. A `moderate`-scope holder ([CC 4.5.5](part_4_composition_governance.md)) enables a watchlist `{id}` for a group they moderate; the fabric auto-fires the matcher at the **publish/share seam** and auto-fires the action (CSAM → `takedown_notice{PerceptualHashCsam}` [CC 4.5.3](part_4_composition_governance.md); other → `detection:*` + ModerationEvent to the named moderator). **Per-group, NEVER global** (a global "scan everything" is the bulk-surveillance posture CIRIS rejects). Enable/disable is signed by the CC 4.5.5 `moderate`/`takedown` authority and revocable by `withdraws`; enabling + every match emit `hard_case:watchlist_enabled` / `:watchlist_match` (never silent). Cannot reach [CC 5.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md) self/family private content (the CC 8.3.2 limit). See [CC 4.5.7](part_4_composition_governance.md). Rides `scores`/config over `delegates_to`; no new primitive.

gist: The scope of a grant is the scope member of the consent:state:granted envelope: a string or array of tokens; a granted naming no scope matches nothing
entry_phrase: **The scope of a grant is the `scope` member of the `consent:state:granted` envelope** — a bare string or an array of tokens naming what the grant covers. A `granted` naming no scope matches nothing, by design. Canonical kinds: `retain` (keep the bytes), `share` (propagate across federation), `analyze` (derive features / scores / classifications), `train` (use as training input), `publish` (publish to external systems). Open vocab with sub-scoping **in the token**: `retain:90d`, `share:cohort:family`. A `consent:scope:{kind}` dimension row, if anyone emits one, is **descriptive** — no fold reads it and it confers nothing; this row stays registered so the family has an owner ([CC 3.1.7](part_3_the_namespace.md) R1). `analyze` governs *continued processing* per [CC 2.3.5](part_2_the_grammar.md) **and is binding on emission for `capacity:*`**: the consent-before-scoring admission gate at [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md) refuses a federation-tier `capacity:*` row whose subject holds no live `analyze` grant addressed to the scoring community.

entry_phrase: **`stance` is a closed-set value** (`granted` / `revoked` / `expired`); **`expired` is substrate-emitted only** — a producer/subject MUST NOT assert `expired` (it is the substrate's `valid_until`-passed emission).

gist: A stance revoked consent_record is not local-tier-eligible; it goes federation-tier hybrid-signed or rides the 24-hour local-to-federation promotion; a self-consent granted with sole authority MAY be local-tier
entry_phrase: **Tier eligibility** per [CC 5.3.2.2](part_5_transport_substrate.md): a `stance: revoked` `consent_record` is **NOT local-tier-eligible** (it carries subject revocation authority over another party's content) — it goes federation-tier (hybrid-signed) or rides the CC 5.3.2.2 24-hour `local → federation` promotion.

gist: A stance revoked consent_record whose subject_key_id is in the target's subject_key_ids[] is admitted under subject-revocation authority; substrate SHOULD record the admitting rule; no cosignature or quorum
entry_phrase: 4. **Composition with the [CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md) `withdraws` gate**: a `stance: revoked` `consent_record` whose `subject_key_id` ∈ the target's `subject_key_ids[]` is admitted under CC 2.4.1.1 subject-revocation authority (rules 2–4). The substrate SHOULD record which rule admitted it (the CC 2.4.1.1 per-rule audit metadata). No producer co-signature and **no quorum** is required — single-subject authority suffices ([CC 4.4.3.5.4](part_4_composition_governance.md)).

gist: A CEG-conforming substrate MUST reject an attestation whose dimension matches a reserved-prefix pattern and whose attesting_key_id fails the emitter rule; rejection is at admission and rejected rows are not stored
entry_phrase: A CEG-Conforming Substrate (CCS) MUST reject any incoming attestation whose `dimension` matches a reserved-prefix pattern below AND whose `attesting_key_id` does not satisfy the prefix's emitter rule.

gist: The reserved-prefix gate is on the dimension and binds every attestation carrying one, delegates_to rows included, checked at the same admission point by the same three actors
entry_phrase: Where a reserved family rides a structural composer, the composer's row is checked at the same admission point, by the same three actors, on the same evidence.

gist: Reserved-prefix matching is longest-pattern: the pattern with more matched literal segments governs; first-segment or shortest-match resolution MUST NOT be used
entry_phrase: Where more than one reserved-prefix pattern matches a `dimension`, the pattern with the **greater number of matched literal segments** governs, and only that pattern's emitter rule is applied.

gist: A producer MUST NOT register a reserved-prefix pattern that would tie another on segment count for one dimension
entry_phrase: Two distinct patterns cannot match the same segment count on the same dimension, because a pattern is a literal segment sequence; a producer MUST NOT register a pattern that would create such a tie.

gist: A CEG-conforming consumer MUST independently re-check the reserved-prefix rule on every received attestation regardless of prior admission; substrate and consumer checks MUST agree
entry_phrase: A CEG-Conforming Consumer (CCC) MUST independently re-check the reserved-prefix rule on every received attestation regardless of whether it was previously admitted by another peer's substrate.

gist: A CEG-conforming producer MUST NOT emit under a reserved prefix unless its attesting_key_id satisfies the emitter rule; violation is a producer-side conformance violation whatever downstream accepts
entry_phrase: A CEG-Conforming Producer (CCP) MUST NOT emit an attestation under a reserved prefix unless its `attesting_key_id` satisfies the emitter rule. Violation is a producer-side conformance violation regardless of whether any downstream substrate accepts the violation.

gist: Every reserved-prefix admission decision MUST be made against the federation_keys row's identity_type set, never a role carried inside a registration envelope
entry_phrase: **The gate reads `identity_type`, never a role carried in a registration envelope.** Every admission decision above MUST be made against the `federation_keys` row's `identity_type` set ([CC 3.4.7.1](part_3_the_namespace.md)).

gist: federation_keys.identity_type is a set of roles; one key MAY hold several identity types at once
entry_phrase: **`federation_keys.identity_type` is a SET of roles, not a single scalar role.** A single federation key MAY simultaneously hold multiple identity types.

gist: A key holding node MUST NOT also hold agent or user; this is the only cohabitation exception
entry_phrase: **One pair is carved out and MUST NOT cohabit: `node` with `agent`, and `node` with `user`** — a key is substrate or actor, never both ([CC 3.4.7.3](part_3_the_namespace.md), which also fixes the gate that this permission would otherwise silently repeal).

gist: Every emitter rule reading identity_type=X is evaluated as X in the key's identity_type set; a key satisfies a reserved-prefix gate iff the required role is among its held roles
entry_phrase: > Wherever a CC 3.4 emitter rule reads "`attesting_key_id` MUST match a `federation_keys` row with `identity_type=X`" (or "`identity_type="X"`"), the normative reading is **`X ∈ attesting_key.identity_type`** — the key's role-set MUST CONTAIN `X`.

gist: A scalar identity_type X is the singleton set {X}; substrates MUST interpret the column as a set and consumers MUST read a scalar as a one-element set
entry_phrase: Substrate implementations MUST interpret the column as a set (its storage form is the implementer's, below); consumers MUST read a scalar as a one-element set.

gist: Where identity_type enters canonical bytes it MUST be encoded as its members sorted ascending by code point, deduplicated, comma-joined without whitespace; a single role encodes as its scalar form
entry_phrase: **Canonical-bytes encoding.** Where `identity_type` enters a canonical-bytes computation (e.g., cross-attestation of a `federation_keys` row), the set MUST be encoded as its members sorted ascending by Unicode code point, deduplicated, comma-joined with no whitespace (e.g., `agent,lenscore_detector`).

gist: identity_type storage is the implementer's choice; a TEXT column holding the comma-joined form decoded on read is conformant; new role values need no schema change
entry_phrase: A single free-form `TEXT` column holding the comma-joined form, decoded-to-set on read, **is conformant** — the comma-joined string *is* the canonical representation, and the set is its interpretation.

gist: Role cohabitation grants the right to emit under each held role's reserved prefixes but does not merge namespaces; shadowing and self-emission rules apply per held role
entry_phrase: **Cohabitation does NOT collapse the dimension split.** Role cohabitation grants a key the *right* to emit under each held role's reserved prefixes; it does NOT merge the roles' namespaces.

gist: A co-located steward role never lets a single node issue a federation-scope attestation; registry consensus is the founder quorum over ciris-canonical; a co-located node gains neither vote nor verdict
entry_phrase: - **Authority stays quorum-bound.** A co-located `steward` role does NOT let a single node issue a federation-scope attestation ([CC 3.2](#3.2)).

gist: lenscore_detector emissions under detection:* are validated not adjudicated and are never sole evidence for an authority action
entry_phrase: - **Observation stays non-authoritative by namespace.** `lenscore_detector` emissions live under `detection:*` and are **validated, not adjudicated** ([CC 1.7](part_1_foundation.md)) — never sole evidence for an authority action ([CC 3.4.8](#3.4.8) / [CC 1.2 T4](part_1_foundation.md)).

gist: Holding both a detector and an authority role cannot make a detection:* emission an authority verdict; authority is quorum-gated upstream of any single key
entry_phrase: - **Observation can never manufacture authority.** Holding both roles cannot make a `detection:*` emission an authority verdict: the namespaces do not merge (above), and authority is quorum-gated *upstream of any single key*.

gist: A fabric node co-locating authority, observation and consensus is conformant iff the above hold; one that converts what it observes into what it can authorize is non-conformant
entry_phrase: A fabric node co-locating authority + observation + consensus is conformant **iff** these hold. An implementation that lets a co-located node convert what it *observes* into what it can *authorize* has broken the separation at that point and is **non-conformant** — fix the wiring, never weaken the rule.

gist: federation_keys.consent_role gates Counter-RII probe detection; its three primitive semantics are fixed here and cannot be set per-consumer
entry_phrase: `federation_keys.consent_role` is the role enum that gates **Counter-RII** probe detection. Three primitive-level semantics shape the substrate's `federation_keys.consent_role` schema and the transport's probe-pattern observer gate, and so **cannot be set per-consumer**; they are fixed here.

gist: consent_role revocation is non-recursive: a later revocation overwrites the prior record; chain history if retained MUST live in a separate audit surface, never embedded in the consent_role JSONB
entry_phrase: Chain history, **if retained**, MUST live in a separate audit surface and **MUST NOT be embedded in the `consent_role` JSONB**.

gist: A key holding the Peer consent_role escapes Counter-RII detection at any trust_mode
entry_phrase: **Peer eligibility: blanket suppression.** A node holding the `Peer` `consent_role` escapes Counter-RII detection at **any** `trust_mode`.

gist: ratchet:flag:counter_rii:{layer} is advisory only and can never be sole evidence for slashing:*; the WA quorum is the adjudication gate
entry_phrase: **Peer eligibility: blanket suppression.** A node holding the `Peer` `consent_role` escapes Counter-RII detection at **any** `trust_mode`.

gist: An AuthorizedReview consent_role is signal-eligible immediately at t greater than window_end with no grace period; reviewers MUST respect their windows
entry_phrase: **Post-window `AuthorizedReview`: strict.** An `AuthorizedReview` `consent_role` is signal-eligible **immediately** at `t > window_end` — no grace period.

gist: Implementations MAY build the consent_role substrate; consent_role is a federation_keys identity field, not an envelope primitive
entry_phrase: Implementations MAY build the `consent_role` substrate. **1+4 untouched** — `consent_role` is a `federation_keys` identity field (sibling to [CC 3.4.7.1](#3.4.7.1) `identity_type`), not an envelope primitive.

gist: When two structural composers race on one references_attestation_id consumers MUST compute a deterministic verdict by the stated precedence
entry_phrase: When two structural composers race on the same `references_attestation_id`, consumers MUST compute a deterministic verdict using the following precedence:

gist: For one attester against one prior row, recants outranks withdraws outranks supersedes regardless of asserted_at
entry_phrase: 1. **`recants` outranks `withdraws` outranks `supersedes`** at the structural level. If the same attester emits multiple composers against the same prior attestation, `recants` wins regardless of `asserted_at` (a falsity admission cannot be subsumed by a retraction or replacement).

gist: For same-type composers by the same attester the largest asserted_at wins within one audience; a widening carries the prior's asserted_at and is a placement, never a competing successor
entry_phrase: 2. **For same-type concurrent emissions by the same attester**: the composer with the largest `asserted_at` per [CC 2.6.2](part_2_the_grammar.md#2.6.2) wins. The ranking applies among rows placed in **one audience** (the same `cohort_scope` target). A widening of one row into a different audience ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md), `widened_at`) carries the prior's `asserted_at` and is a placement, never a competing successor, so widenings are not ranked against each other.

gist: For equal asserted_at the row with the bytewise-lowest attestation_id wins; both rows stay stored and the rank is read-time
entry_phrase: 3. **For same-`asserted_at` ties**: the composer whose row's `attestation_id` is lowest, compared bytewise, wins, so every node orders the tie the same way. Both rows stay stored; the rank is read-time.

gist: For cross-attester composers on one prior row each attester's chain is evaluated independently and the consumer applies 4.4 policy over N parallel chains
entry_phrase: **For cross-attester emissions on the same `references_attestation_id`**: each attester's chain is evaluated independently; the consumer sees N parallel chains and applies [CC 4.4](part_4_composition_governance.md#4.4) policy.

gist: Structural composers are idempotent on attestation_id: a replay is a no-op; a distinct same-type row from one attester on one target is ranked within its audience; the loser is kept
entry_phrase: Structural composers are idempotent on the row's `attestation_id`: a replay of the same row is a no-op. A distinct row of the same type from the same attester on the same target is not a replay. Rules 2–3 rank it within its audience, so every node converges on the same winner whichever row it held first. The losing row is kept, not evicted.

gist: Consumer policy must treat the Contribution as revoked for all subjects; no majority or all-must-agree softening
entry_phrase: any one subject's terminal `withdraws` evicts `T` for all (the any-subject-binding above).

gist: Under an erasure_exempt affiliation class or legal_hold the withdraws is admitted and recorded but the descent is refused with reason; the subject's path is 4.5.5
entry_phrase: Where `T` is held under an affiliation class flagged `erasure_exempt` or under a `legal_hold` ([CC 4.4.3.2.8](#4.4.3.2.8)), the `withdraws` is admitted and recorded, and the descent it would force is refused with reason under that declared gate. The subject's path is [CC 4.5.5](#4.5.5).

gist: A contract under erasure_exempt or legal_hold: withdrawal recorded, descent refused with reason
entry_phrase: Where the contract is held under `erasure_exempt` or a `legal_hold`, the withdrawal is recorded and the descent is refused with reason ([CC 4.4.3.2.8](#4.4.3.2.8)); the signatory's path is [CC 4.5.5](#4.5.5).

gist: Producers may partition content into per-subject Contributions so one subject's revocation does not evict another's content
entry_phrase: Producers MAY mitigate by partitioning content into per-subject Contributions (e.g., one chat-message Contribution per author, linked via `topical_relation:replies_to`) so that one subject's revocation doesn't evict another's content.

gist: A per-subject withdraws is admitted exactly as a single-subject one; the rule does not change for more subjects
entry_phrase: **(1) admission** — the per-subject `withdraws` is admitted under [CC 2.4.1.1 rule 2/3](part_2_the_grammar.md) exactly as a single-subject `withdraws` is.

gist: Latest-wins and revoke-is-terminal apply per subject; any one subject's terminal withdraws evicts for all

gist: There is no separate evict event: the withdrawal is the evict; substrates implement the OR over per-subject revocation state
entry_phrase: Substrates implement this as the OR over per-subject revocation state, not as a new code path.

gist: The L1-L5 ladder is consumer-side composition over mechanism prefixes, not a wire taxonomy
entry_phrase: The familiar L1-L5 verification "ladder" (self_verify → hardware_rooted → registry_consensus → license_validity → agent_integrity) is **consumer-side composition over the mechanism prefixes** in [CC 3.1.2](part_3_the_namespace.md), not a wire-level taxonomy.

gist: The wire carries the mechanism prefix, never the ladder position
entry_phrase: Per [CC 1.2](part_1_foundation.md) T2 honestly applied: the L-number names a *ladder position* (a verdict-shape consumers compute), not a *mechanism* (which is what the wire MUST carry).

gist: Consumers map self_verify, hardware_rooted, registry_consensus, license_validity, agent_integrity to L1 through L5 in that order
entry_phrase: The familiar L1-L5 verification "ladder" (self_verify → hardware_rooted → registry_consensus → license_validity → agent_integrity) is **consumer-side composition over the mechanism prefixes** in [CC 3.1.2](part_3_the_namespace.md), not a wire-level taxonomy.

entry_phrase: if any positive attestation on attestation:{prefix}:
